421 void
422 whatTypeOfFileIsThis( const string & name )
423  {
424  // DQ (2/3/2009): It is helpful to report what type of file this is where possible.
425  // Call the Unix "file" command, it would be great if this was an available
426  // system call (but Robb thinks it might not always be available).
427 
428  vector<string> commandLineVector;
429  commandLineVector.push_back("file -b " + name);
430 
431  printf ("Error: unknown file type: ");
432  flush(cout);
433 
434  // Use "-b" for brief mode!
435  string commandLine = "file " + name;
436  if (system(commandLine.c_str()))
437  mlog[ERROR] <<"command failed: \"" <<StringUtility::cEscape(commandLine) <<"\"\n";
438  }

476 string
477 findRoseSupportPathFromBuild(const string& buildTreeLocation,
478  const string& installTreeLocation) {
479  string installTreePath;
480  bool inInstallTree = roseInstallPrefix(installTreePath);
481  if (inInstallTree) {
482  return installTreePath + "/" + installTreeLocation;
483  } else {
484  #ifdef _MSC_VER
485  #ifndef CMAKE_INTDIR
486  #define CMAKE_INTDIR ""
487  #endif
488  if (buildTreeLocation.compare(0, 3, "lib") == 0 || buildTreeLocation.compare(0, 3, "bin") == 0) {
489  return string(ROSE_AUTOMAKE_TOP_BUILDDIR) + "/" + buildTreeLocation + "/" + CMAKE_INTDIR;
490  }
491  #endif
492  return string(ROSE_AUTOMAKE_TOP_BUILDDIR) + "/" + buildTreeLocation;
493  }
494 }
496 // There are two ways
497 // 1. if dladdr is supported: we resolve a rose function (roseInstallPrefix()) to obtain the
498 // file (librose.so) defining this function
499 // Then we check the parent directory of librose.so
500 // if .libs or src --> in a build tree
501 // otherwise: librose.so is in an installation tree
502 // 2. if dladdr is not supported or anything goes wrong, we check an environment variable
503 // ROSE_IN_BUILD_TREE to tell if the translator is started from a build tree or an installation tree
504 // Otherwise we pass the --prefix= ROSE_AUTOMAKE_PREFIX as the installation prefix
505 bool roseInstallPrefix(std::string& result) {
506 #ifdef HAVE_DLADDR
507  {
508  // This is built on the stack and initialized using the function: dladdr().
509  Dl_info info;
510 
511  // DQ (4/8/2011): Initialize this before it is used as a argument to strdup() below. This is initialized
512  // by dladdr(), so this is likely redundant; but we can initialize it anyway.
513  // info.dli_fname = NULL;
514  info.dli_fname = "";
515 
516  int retval = dladdr((void*)(&roseInstallPrefix), &info);
517  if (retval == 0) goto default_check;
518 
519  // DQ (4/9/2011): I think the issue here is that the pointer "info.dli_fname" pointer (char*) is pointing to
520  // a position inside a DLL and thus is a region of memory controled/monitored or allocated by Insure++. Thus
521  // Insure++ is marking this as an issue while it is not an issue. The reported issue by Insure++ is: "READ_WILD",
522  // implying that a pointer set to some wild area of memory is being read.
523 #if __INSURE__
524  // Debugging information. Trying to understand this insure issue and the value of "info.dli_fname" data member.
525  // if (retval != 0)
526  // fprintf(stderr, " %08p file: %s\tfunction: %s\n",info.dli_saddr, info.dli_fname ? info.dli_fname : "???", info.dli_sname ? info.dli_sname : "???");
527 
528  _Insure_checking_enable(0); // disable Insure++ checking
529 #endif
530  // DQ (4/8/2011): Check for NULL pointer before handling it as a parameter to strdup(),
531  // but I think it is always non-NULL (added assertion and put back the original code).
532  // char* libroseName = (info.dli_fname == NULL) ? NULL : strdup(info.dli_fname);
533  ASSERT_not_null(info.dli_fname);
534  char* libroseName = strdup(info.dli_fname);
535 #if __INSURE__
536  _Insure_checking_enable(1); // re-enable Insure++ checking
537 #endif
538 
539  if (libroseName == nullptr) goto default_check;
540  char* libdir = dirname(libroseName);
541  if (libdir == nullptr) {free(libroseName); goto default_check;}
542  char* libdirCopy1 = strdup(libdir);
543  char* libdirCopy2 = strdup(libdir);
544  if (libdirCopy1 == nullptr || libdirCopy2 == nullptr) { free(libroseName); free(libdirCopy1); free(libdirCopy2); goto default_check;}
545  char* libdirBasenameCS = basename(libdirCopy1);
546  if (libdirBasenameCS == nullptr) {free(libroseName); free(libdirCopy1); free(libdirCopy2); goto default_check;}
547  string libdirBasename = libdirBasenameCS;
548  free(libdirCopy1);
549  char* prefixCS = dirname(libdirCopy2);
550  if (prefixCS == nullptr) {free(libroseName); goto default_check;}
551  string prefix = prefixCS;
552  free(libdirCopy2);
553 
554  // Zack Galbreath, June 2013
555  // When building with CMake, detect build directory by searching
556  // for the presence of a CMakeCache.txt file. If this cannot
557  // be found, then assume we are running from within an install tree.
558  // Pei-Hung (04/08/21) use prefix to find CMakeCache.txt and return ROSE_AUTOMAKE_PREFIX if installation is used
559  #ifdef USE_CMAKE
560  std::string pathToCache = prefix;
561  pathToCache += "/CMakeCache.txt";
562  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
563  printf ("Inside of roseInstallPrefix libdir = %s pathToCache = %s \n",libdir, pathToCache.c_str());
564  if (boost::filesystem::exists(pathToCache)) {
565  return false;
566  } else {
567  result = ROSE_AUTOMAKE_PREFIX;
568  return true;
569  }
570  #endif
571 
572  free(libroseName);
573 // Liao, 12/2/2009
574 // Check the librose's parent directory name to tell if it is within a build or installation tree
575 // This if statement has the assumption that libtool is used to build librose so librose.so is put under .libs
576 // which is not true for cmake building system
577 // For cmake, librose is created directly under build/src
578  if (libdirBasename == ".libs" || libdirBasename == "src") {
579  return false;
580  } else {
581  // the translator must locate in the installation_tree/lib
582  if (libdirBasename != "lib" && libdirBasename != "lib64")
583  {
584  printf ("Error: unexpected libdirBasename = %s (result = %s, prefix = %s) \n",libdirBasename.c_str(),result.c_str(),prefix.c_str());
585  }
586 
587  result = prefix;
588  return true;
589  }
590  }
591 #endif
592 default_check:
593 #ifdef HAVE_DLADDR
594  // Emit a warning that the hard-wired prefix is being used
595  cerr << "Warning: roseInstallPrefix() is using the hard-wired prefix and ROSE_IN_BUILD_TREE even though it should be relocatable" << endl;
596 #endif
597  // dladdr is not supported, we check an environment variables to tell if the
598  // translator is running from a build tree or an installation tree
599  if (getenv("ROSE_IN_BUILD_TREE") != nullptr) {
600  return false;
601  } else {
602 // Liao, 12/1/2009
603 // this variable is set via a very bad way, there is actually a right way to use --prefix VALUE within automake/autoconfig
604 // config/build_rose_paths.Makefile
605 // Makefile: @@echo "const std::string ROSE_AUTOMAKE_PREFIX = \"/home/liao6/opt/roseLatest\";" >> src/util/rose_paths.C

612 /* This function suffers from the same problems as CommandlineProcessing::isExecutableFilename(), namely that the list of
613  * magic numbers used here needs to be kept in sync with changes to the binary parsers. */
614 bool
615 isBinaryExecutableFile ( string sourceFilename )
616  {
617  bool returnValue = false;
618 
619  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
620  printf ("Inside of isBinaryExecutableFile(%s) \n",sourceFilename.c_str());
621 
622  // Open file for reading
623  FILE* f = fopen(sourceFilename.c_str(), "rb");
624  if (!f)
625  return false; // a file that cannot be opened is not a binary file
626 
627  int character0 = fgetc(f);
628  int character1 = fgetc(f);
629 
630  // The first character of an ELF binary is '\127' and for a PE binary it is 'M'
631  // Note also that some MS-DOS headers can start with "ZM" instead of "MZ" due to
632  // early confusion about little endian handling for MS-DOS where it was ported
633  // to not x86 plaforms. I am not clear how wide spread loaders of this type are.
634 
635  if (character0 == 127 || character0 == 77)
636  {
637  if (character1 == 'E' || character1 == 'Z')
638  {
639  returnValue = true;
640  }
641  }
642 
643  fclose(f);
644 
645  return returnValue;
646  }
647 
648 bool
649 isLibraryArchiveFile ( string sourceFilename )
650  {
651  // The if this is a "*.a" file, not that "*.so" files
652  // will appear as an executable (same for Windows "*.dll"
653  // files.
654 
655  bool returnValue = false;
656 
657  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 ) {
658  printf ("Inside of isLibraryArchiveFile(%s) \n",sourceFilename.c_str());
659  }
660 
661  // Open file for reading
662  FILE* f = fopen(sourceFilename.c_str(), "rb");
663  if (!f) {
664  return false; // a non-existing file is not a library archive
665  }
666 
667  string magicHeader;
668  for (int i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
669  magicHeader = magicHeader + (char)getc(f);
670  }
671 
672  returnValue = (magicHeader == "!<arch>");
673  fclose(f);
674 
675  return returnValue;
676  }

691 void
692 SgSourceFile::initializeGlobalScope()
693  {
694  ASSERT_not_null(get_startOfConstruct());
695 
696  string sourceFilename = get_startOfConstruct()->get_filename();
697  Sg_File_Info* globalScopeFileInfo = new Sg_File_Info(sourceFilename,0,0);
698  ASSERT_not_null(globalScopeFileInfo);
699 
700  set_globalScope(new SgGlobal(globalScopeFileInfo));
701  ASSERT_not_null(get_globalScope());
702 
703  if (SageInterface::is_language_case_insensitive())
704  {
705  ASSERT_require(SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics == true);
706  get_globalScope()->setCaseInsensitive(true);
707  }
708 
709  get_globalScope()->set_parent(this);
710 
711  // DQ (8/21/2008): Set the end of the global scope (even if it is updated later)
712  ASSERT_require(get_globalScope()->get_endOfConstruct() == nullptr);
713  get_globalScope()->set_endOfConstruct(new Sg_File_Info(sourceFilename,0,0));
714 
715  ASSERT_not_null(get_globalScope()->get_startOfConstruct());
716  ASSERT_not_null(get_globalScope()->get_endOfConstruct());
717 
718  // DQ (12/22/2008): Added to support CPP preprocessing of Fortran files.
719  string filename = p_sourceFileNameWithPath;
720  if (get_requires_C_preprocessor() == true)
721  {
722  // This must be a Fortran source file (requiring the use of CPP to process its directives).
723  filename = generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename(filename);
724  }
725 
726  get_globalScope()->get_startOfConstruct()->set_filenameString(filename);
727  ASSERT_require(get_globalScope()->get_startOfConstruct()->get_filenameString().empty() == false);
728 
729  get_globalScope()->get_endOfConstruct()->set_filenameString(filename);
730  ASSERT_require(get_globalScope()->get_endOfConstruct()->get_filenameString().empty() == false);
731 
732  // DQ (12/23/2008): These should be in the Sg_File_Info map already.
733  ASSERT_require(Sg_File_Info::getIDFromFilename(get_file_info()->get_filename()) >= 0);
734  if (get_requires_C_preprocessor() == true)
735  {
736  ASSERT_require(Sg_File_Info::getIDFromFilename(generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename(get_file_info()->get_filename())) >= 0);
737  }
738  }

740 SgFile*
741 determineFileType(vector<string> argv, int & /*nextErrorCode*/, SgProject* project)
742  {
743  SgFile* file = nullptr;
744 
745  ASSERT_not_null(project);
746  Rose_STL_Container<string> fileList = CommandlineProcessing::generateSourceFilenames(argv,project->get_binary_only());
747 
748  ROSE_ASSERT(fileList.empty() == false);
749 
750  if (fileList.empty() == false)
751  {
752  if (fileList.size() != 1){
753  cout << endl;
754  for ( Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator i = fileList.begin(); i != fileList.end(); i++) {
755  cout << (*i) << endl;
756  }
757  cout << endl;
758  cout.flush();
759  }
760  ROSE_ASSERT(fileList.size() == 1);
761 
762  // DQ (8/31/2006): Convert the source file to have a path if it does not already
763  string sourceFilename = *(fileList.begin());
764  sourceFilename = StringUtility::getAbsolutePathFromRelativePath(sourceFilename, true);
765 
766  // This should be an absolute path
767  string targetSubstring = "/";
768 
769  // Zack Galbreath 1/9/2014: Windows absolute paths do not begin with "/".
770  // The following printf could cause problems for our testing systems because
771  // it contains the word "error".
772  // [Robb P Matzke 2017-04-21]: Such a low-level utility function as this shouldn't be emitting output at all, especially
773  // not on standard output, because it makes it problematic to call this in situations where the file might not
774  // exist.
775  #ifndef _MSC_VER
776  //if (sourceFilename.substr(0,targetSubstring.size()) != targetSubstring)
777  // printf ("sourceFilename encountered an error in filename\n");
778  #endif
779 
780  string filenameExtension = StringUtility::fileNameSuffix(sourceFilename);
781 
782  // DQ (1/8/2014): We need to handle the case of "/dev/null" being used as an input filename.
783  if (filenameExtension == "/dev/null")
784  {
785  printf ("Warning: detected use of /dev/null as input filename: not yet supported (exiting with 0 exit code) \n");
786  exit(0);
787  }
788 
789  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortranFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
790  {
791  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile(argv, project);
792  file = sourceFile;
793 
794 #ifdef ROSE_EXPERIMENTAL_FLANG_ROSE_CONNECTION
795  file->set_experimental_flang_frontend(true);
796 #endif
797 
798  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortranFileExtension(true);
799  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Fortran_language);
800  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Fortran_language);
801 
802  file->set_Fortran_only(true);
803  Rose::is_Fortran_language = true;
804 
805  SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics = true;
806  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
807 
808  // determine whether to run this file through the C preprocessor
809  bool requires_C_preprocessor =
810  // DXN (02/20/2011): rmod file should never require it
811  (filenameExtension != "rmod")
812  &&
813  (
814  // if the file extension implies it
815  CommandlineProcessing::isFortranFileNameSuffixRequiringCPP(filenameExtension)
816  ||
817  //if the command line includes "-D" options
818  ! getProject()->get_macroSpecifierList().empty()
819  );
820 
821  if (file->get_experimental_flang_frontend() == true) {
822  // Don't do C++ stuff for Flang frontend
823  file->set_requires_C_preprocessor(false);
824  file->set_disable_edg_backend(true);
825  file->set_skip_commentsAndDirectives(true);
826  }
827  else {
828  file->set_requires_C_preprocessor(requires_C_preprocessor);
829  }
830 
831  // DQ (12/23/2008): This needs to be called after the set_requires_C_preprocessor() function is called.
832  // If CPP processing is required then the global scope should have a source position using the intermediate
833  // file name (generated by generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename()).
834  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
835 
836  // Now set the specific types of Fortran file extensions
837  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortran77FileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
838  {
839  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortran77FileExtension(true);
840  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_fixed_form_output_format);
841  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_fixed_form_output_format);
842  file->set_F77_only();
843  }
844 
845  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortran90FileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
846  {
847  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortran90FileExtension(true);
848  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
849  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
850  file->set_F90_only();
851  }
852 
853  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortran95FileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
854  {
855  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortran95FileExtension(true);
856  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
857  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
858  file->set_F95_only();
859  }
860 
861  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortran2003FileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
862  {
863  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortran2003FileExtension(true);
864  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
865  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
866  file->set_F2003_only();
867  }
868 
869  if (CommandlineProcessing::isCoArrayFortranFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
870  {
871  file->set_sourceFileUsesCoArrayFortranFileExtension(true);
872  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
873  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
874  file->set_F2003_only();
875  file->set_CoArrayFortran_only(true);
876  }
877 
878  if (CommandlineProcessing::isFortran2008FileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
879  {
880  file->set_sourceFileUsesFortran2008FileExtension(true);
881  file->set_outputFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
882  file->set_backendCompileFormat(SgFile::e_free_form_output_format);
883  file->set_F2008_only();
884  }
885  }
886  else
887  {
888  // SG (7/9/2015) When processing multiple files, we need to reset
889  // case_insensitive_semantics. But this only sets it to the last
890  // file created. During AST construction, it will need to be
891  // reset for each language.
892  SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics = false;
893 
894  if (CommandlineProcessing::isPHPFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
895  {
896  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
897  file = sourceFile;
898 
899  file->set_sourceFileUsesPHPFileExtension(true);
900  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_PHP_language);
901  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_PHP_language);
902  file->set_PHP_only(true);
903 
904  Rose::is_PHP_language = true;
905 
906  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
907  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
908  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
909  }
910  else
911  {
912  if (CommandlineProcessing::isCppFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
913  {
914  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
915  file = sourceFile;
916 
917  // This is a C++ file (so define __cplusplus, just like GNU gcc would)
918  file->set_sourceFileUsesCppFileExtension(true);
919 
920  // Use the filename suffix as a default means to set this value
921  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Cxx_language);
922  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Cxx_language);
923  file->set_Cxx_only(true);
924 
925  Rose::is_Cxx_language = true;
926 
927  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
928  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
929  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
930  }
931  else
932  {
933  // Liao, 6/6/2008, Assume AST with UPC will be unparsed using the C unparser
934  if ( ( CommandlineProcessing::isCFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true ) ||
935  ( CommandlineProcessing::isUPCFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true ) )
936  {
937  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
938  file = sourceFile;
939 
940  // This a not a C++ file (assume it is a C file and don't define the __cplusplus macro, just like GNU gcc would)
941  file->set_sourceFileUsesCppFileExtension(false);
942 
943  // Use the filename suffix as a default means to set this value
944  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_C_language);
945 
946  // DQ (8/29/2017): Set the input language as well.
947  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_C_language);
948 
949  file->set_C_only(true);
950 
951  // DQ (11/25/2020): Add support to set this as a specific language kind file (there is at least one language kind file processed by ROSE).
952  Rose::is_C_language = true;
953 
954  // Liao 6/6/2008 Set the newly introduced p_UPC_only flag.
955  if (CommandlineProcessing::isUPCFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
956  {
957  file->set_UPC_only();
958  Rose::is_UPC_language = true;
959  }
960  else
961  {
962  file->set_C99_gnu_only();
963  }
964 
965  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
966  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
967  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
968  }
969  else
970  {
971  if ( CommandlineProcessing::isCudaFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true )
972  {
973  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
974  file = sourceFile;
975 
976  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Cxx_language);
977  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Cxx_language);
978  file->set_Cuda_only(true);
979  Rose::is_Cuda_language = true;
980 
981  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
982  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
983  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
984  }
985  else if ( CommandlineProcessing::isOpenCLFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true )
986  {
987  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
988  file = sourceFile;
989  file->set_OpenCL_only(true);
990  Rose::is_OpenCL_language = true;
991 
992  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
993  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
994  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
995  }
996  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isJavaFile(sourceFilename))
997  {
998  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile(argv, project);
999  file = sourceFile;
1000  file->set_sourceFileUsesCppFileExtension(false);
1001  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Java_language);
1002  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Java_language);
1003  file->set_Java_only(true);
1004 
1005  Rose::is_Java_language = true;
1006 
1007  file->set_compileOnly(true);
1008  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
1009  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
1010  }
1011  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isPythonFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
1012  {
1013  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
1014  file = sourceFile;
1015 
1016  file->set_sourceFileUsesPythonFileExtension(true);
1017  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Python_language);
1018  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Python_language);
1019  file->set_Python_only(true);
1020 
1021  Rose::is_Python_language = true;
1022 
1023  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
1024  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
1025  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
1026  }
1027  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isCsharpFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
1028  {
1029  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
1030  file = sourceFile;
1031 
1032  file->set_sourceFileUsesCsharpFileExtension(true);
1033  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Csharp_language);
1034  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Csharp_language);
1035  file->set_Csharp_only(true);
1036 
1037  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
1038  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
1039  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
1040  }
1041  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isAdaFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
1042  {
1043  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile ( argv, project );
1044  file = sourceFile;
1045 
1046  file->set_sourceFileUsesAdaFileExtension(true);
1047  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Ada_language);
1048  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Ada_language);
1049  file->set_Ada_only(true);
1050 
1051  Rose::is_Ada_language = true;
1052 
1053  // PP (04/24/2020)
1054  SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics = true;
1055 
1056  // DQ (12/23/2008): This is the earliest point where the global scope can be set.
1057  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
1058  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
1059  }
1060 
1061  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isJovialFileNameSuffix(filenameExtension) == true)
1062  {
1063  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = new SgSourceFile(argv, project);
1064  file = sourceFile;
1065 
1066  file->set_sourceFileUsesJovialFileExtension(true);
1067  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Jovial_language);
1068  file->set_inputLanguage (SgFile::e_Jovial_language);
1069 
1070  // Don't do C++ stuff
1071  file->set_requires_C_preprocessor(false);
1072  file->set_disable_edg_backend(true);
1073  file->set_skip_commentsAndDirectives(true);
1074 
1075  file->set_Jovial_only(true);
1076  Rose::is_Jovial_language = true;

1078  SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics = true;
1079  sourceFile->initializeGlobalScope();
1080  }
1081 
1082 #ifdef ROSE_ENABLE_BINARY_ANALYSIS
1083  else if (CommandlineProcessing::isJavaJvmFile(sourceFilename))
1084  {
1085  file = new SgJvmComposite(argv, project);
1086  Rose::is_Jvm_language = true;
1087  }
1088  else if (true)
1089  {
1090  // This is not a source file recognized by ROSE, so it is either a binary executable or
1091  // library archive or something that we can't process.
1092  static bool didWarn = false;
1093  if (!didWarn) {
1094  mlog[WARN]
1095  <<"global \"::frontend\" is being used for parsing binary analysis inputs\n"
1096  <<" It is better to use the Rose::BinaryAnaysis::Partitioner2::Engine interface\n"
1097  <<" which is dedicated to binary analysis and has more features and better\n"
1098  <<" control over the details. The closest replacement to \"::frontend\" is\n"
1099  <<" Rose::BinaryAnalysis::Partitioner2::Engine::frontend.\n";
1100  didWarn = true;
1101  }
1102 
1103  // Build a SgBinaryComposite to represent either the binary executable or the library
1104  // archive.
1105  SgBinaryComposite *binary = new SgBinaryComposite(argv, project);
1106  file = binary;
1107  file->set_sourceFileUsesBinaryFileExtension(true);
1108  file->set_outputLanguage(SgFile::e_Binary_language);
1109  file->set_inputLanguage(SgFile::e_Binary_language);
1110 
1111  // If this is an object file being processed for binary analysis then mark it as an object
1112  // file so that we can trigger analysis to mark the sections that will be disassembled.
1113  string binaryFileName = file->get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
1114  if (CommandlineProcessing::isObjectFilename(binaryFileName)) {
1115  file->set_isObjectFile(true);
1116  }
1117 
1118  file->set_binary_only(true);
1119  Rose::is_binary_executable = true;
1120 
1121  file->set_requires_C_preprocessor(false);
1122  ASSERT_not_null(file->get_file_info());
1123 
1124  if (isLibraryArchiveFile(sourceFilename)) {
1125  // WARNING: Static archives aren't handled correctly here (called from ::frontend)
1126  // because we're already at too low a level in the call chain to really do things
1127  // properly. They should have been either linked to form an executable or replaced by a
1128  // list of object files that all go into one SgAsmInterpretation. It's better to handle
1129  // binary analysis command-line arguments with the
1130  // Rose::BinaryAnalysis::Partitioner2::Engine interface.
1131 #ifdef _MSC_VER
1132  /* The following block of code deals with *.a library archives files found on Unix
1133  * systems. I added better temporary file and directory names, but this block of code
1134  * also has commands that likely won't run on Windows systems, so I'm commenting out the
1135  * whole block. [RPM 2010-11-03] */
1136  ASSERT_not_implemented("Windows not supported");
1137 #endif
1138  // This is the case of processing a library archive (*.a) file. We want to process these
1139  // files so that we can test the library identification mechanism to build databases of
1140  // the binary functions in libraries (so that we detect these in staticaly linked
1141  // binaries).
1142  ROSE_ASSERT(!isBinaryExecutableFile(sourceFilename));
1143 
1144  // Note that since a archive can contain many *.o files each of these will be a
1145  // SgAsmGenericFile object and the SgBinaryComposite will contain a list of
1146  // SgAsmGenericFile objects to hold them all.
1147  string archiveName = file->get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
1148  file->set_isLibraryArchive(true);
1149 
1150  // Extract the archive into a temporary directory and create a file in that directory
1151  // that will have the names of objects stored in the archive. We have to be careful
1152  // about name choices since this function could be called multiple times from one
1153  // process, and by multiple processes.
1154  boost::filesystem::path tmpDirectory =
1155  boost::filesystem::temp_directory_path() / boost::filesystem::unique_path();
1156  boost::filesystem::create_directory(tmpDirectory);
1157  std::vector<boost::filesystem::path> memberNames =
1158  BinaryAnalysis::Partitioner2::ModulesElf::extractStaticArchive(tmpDirectory,
1159  archiveName);
1160  for (const boost::filesystem::path &memberName : memberNames)
1161  binary->get_libraryArchiveObjectFileNameList().push_back(memberName.string());
1162  }
1163  }
1164 #endif //ROSE_ENABLE_BINARY_ANALYSIS
1165 
1166  else
1167  {
1168  file = new SgUnknownFile(argv, project);
1169 
1170  ASSERT_not_null(file->get_parent());
1171  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_parent() == project);
1172 
1173  // If all else fails, then output the type of file and exit.
1174  file->set_sourceFileTypeIsUnknown(true);
1175  file->set_requires_C_preprocessor(false);
1176 
1177  ASSERT_not_null(file->get_file_info());
1178  printf("Warning: This is an unknown file type, not being processed by ROSE: sourceFilename = %s \n",
1179  sourceFilename.c_str());
1180  outputTypeOfFileAndExit(sourceFilename);
1181  }
1182  }

1190  // the integer values instead of string comparisons. Required for the handling of CPP directives and comments.

1372 
1373 // DQ (4/10/2017): Not clear if we want to sue this concept of switch setting in ROSE command line handling (implemented as a test).
1374 // Switches for this tool. Tools with lots of switches will probably want these to be in some Settings struct mirroring the
1375 // approach used by some analyses that have lots of settings. So we'll do that here too even though it looks funny.

1385 // DQ (4/10/2017): Added commandline support from Saywer (most comments are from Robb's definition of this function for the tutorial/outliner.cc).
1386 std::vector<std::string>
1387 SgProject::parseCommandLine(std::vector<std::string> argv)
1388  {
1389  // Parse the tool's command-line, processing only those switches recognized by Sawyer. Then return the non-parsed switches for
1390  // the next stage of parsing. We have three more stages that need to process the command-line: Outliner (the old approach),
1391  // frontend(), and the backend compiler. None of these except the backend compiler can issue error messages about misspelled
1392  // switches because the first three must assume that an unrecognized switch is intended for a later stage.
1393 
1394  using namespace Sawyer::CommandLine;
1395 
1396  using namespace Rose; // the ROSE team is migrating everything to this namespace
1397  using namespace Rose::Diagnostics; // for mlog, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL, etc.
1398 
1399  // Use Rose::CommandLine to create a consistent parser among all tools. If you want a tool's parser to be different
1400  // then either create one yourself, or modify the parser properties after createParser returns. The createEmptyParserStage
1401  // creates a parser that assumes all unrecognized switches are intended for a later stage. If there are no later stages
1402  // then use createEmptyParser instead or else users will never see error messages for misspelled switches.
1403  Parser p = Rose::CommandLine::createEmptyParserStage(purpose, description);
1404  p.doc("Synopsis", "@prop{programName} @v{switches} @v{files}...");
1405 
1406  // DEBUGGING [Robb P Matzke 2016-09-27]
1407  p.longPrefix("-");
1408 
1409  // User errors (what few will be reported since this is only a first-stage parser) should be sent to standard error instead
1410  // of raising an exception. Programmer errors still cause exceptions.
1411  p.errorStream(SageBuilder::mlog[FATAL]);
1412 
1413  // All ROSE tools have some switches in common, such as --version, -V, --help, -h, -?, --log, -L, --threads, etc. We
1414  // include them first so they appear near the top of the documentation. The genericSwitches returns a
1415  // Sawyer::CommandLine::SwitchGroup, which this tool could extend by adding additional switches. This could have been done
1416  // inside createParser, but it turns out that many tools like to extend or re-order this group of switches, which is
1417  // simpler this way.
1418  p.with(Rose::CommandLine::genericSwitches());
1419 
1420  // Eventually, if we change frontend so we can query what switches it knows about, we could insert them into our parser at
1421  // this point. The frontend could report all known switches (sort of how things are organized one) or we could query only
1422  // those groups of frontend switches that this tool is interested in (e.g., I don't know if the outliner needs Fortran
1423  // switches).
1424  // [Robb P Matzke 2016-09-27]
1425  p.with(SgProject::frontendAllSwitches()); // or similar
1426 
1427  // DQ (4/10/2017): Added separate function for backend command line switches.
1428  p.with(SgProject::backendAllSwitches()); // or similar
1429 
1430  // Finally, a tool sometimes has its own specific settings, so we demo that here with a couple made-up switches.
1431  SwitchGroup tool("Tool-specific switches");
1432 
1433  tool.insert(Switch("dry-run", 'n')
1434  .intrinsicValue(true, rose_settings.showRoseSettings)
1435  .doc("Instead of running the outliner, just display its settings."));
1436 
1437  // Helper function that adds "--old-outliner" and "--no-old-outliner" to the tool switch group, and causes
1438  // settings.useOldParser to be set to true or false. It also appends some additional documentation to say what the default
1439  // value is. We could have done this by hand with Sawyer, but having a helper encourages consistency.
1440  Rose::CommandLine::insertBooleanSwitch(tool, "old-commandline-handling", rose_settings.useOldCommandlineParser,
1441  "Call the old ROSE frontend command line parser in addition to its new Sawyer parser.");
1442 
1443  // We want the "--rose:help" switch to appear in the Sawyer documentation but we have to pass it to the next stage also. We
1444  // could do this two different ways. The older way (that still works) is to have Sawyer process the switch and then we
1445  // prepend it into the returned vector for processing by later stages. The newer way is to set the switch's "skipping"
1446  // property that causes Sawyer to treat it as a skipped (unrecognized) switch. We'll use SKIP_STRONG, but SKIP_WEAK is
1447  // sort of a cross between Sawyer recognizing it and not recognizing it.
1448  tool.insert(Switch("rose:help")
1449  .skipping(SKIP_STRONG) // appears in documentation and is parsed, but treated as skipped
1450  .doc("Show the non-Sawyer switch documentation."));
1451 
1452  // Note that the apply function is not called
1453  std::vector<std::string> remainingArgs = p.parse(argv).unparsedArgs(true);
1454 
1455 #if ROSE_SAWYER_COMMENT_LINE_DEBUG
1456  // DEBUGGING [Robb P Matzke 2016-09-27]
1457  std::cerr <<"These are the arguments left over after parsing with Sawyer:\n";
1458  for (const std::string &s : remainingArgs)
1459  std::cerr <<" \"" <<s <<"\"\n";
1460 #endif
1461 
1462  return remainingArgs;
1463  }

1467 int
1468 SgProject::parse(const vector<string>& argv)
1469  {
1470  // Not sure that if we are just linking that we should call a function called "parse()"!!!
1471 
1472  // DQ (7/6/2005): Introduce tracking of performance of ROSE.
1473  TimingPerformance timer ("AST (SgProject::parse(argc,argv)):");
1474 
1475  // DQ (4/10/2017): Experiment with Saywer for comment line parsing.
1476  // Parse Sawyer-recognized switches and the rest we'll pass to Outliner and frontend like before.
1477  std::vector<std::string> sawyer_args = parseCommandLine(argv);
1478 
1479 #if 0
1480  // Unclear if we want to use this feature of Sawyer.
1481  if (rose_settings.useOldCommandlineParser)
1482  {
1483  // Example of usage from outliner.

1485 
1486  printf ("In SgProject::parse(): Permit optional command line handling using the older approach (not supported) \n");

1489 
1490  // TOO1 (2014/01/22): TODO: Consider moving CLI processing out of SgProject
1491  // constructor. We can't set any error codes on SgProject since SgProject::parse
1492  // is being called from the SgProject::SgProject constructor, meaning the SgProject
1493  // object is not properly constructed yet.. The only thing we can do, then, if
1494  // there is an error here in the commandline handling, is to halt the program.
1495  if (KEEP_GOING_CAUGHT_COMMANDLINE_SIGNAL)
1496  {
1497  std::cout
1498  << "[FATAL] "
1499  << "Unrecoverable signal generated during commandline processing"
1500  << std::endl;
1501  exit(1);
1502  }
1503  else
1504  {
1505  // builds file list (or none if this is a link line)
1506  processCommandLine(argv);
1507  }
1508 
1509  int errorCode = 0;
1510 
1511  // Normal case without AST Merge: Compiling ...
1512  if (get_sourceFileNameList().size() > 0)
1513  {
1514 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
1515  // Start the Java Native Interface (JNI) server for either Fortran or Java
1516  Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::jserver_init();
1517 #endif
1518  //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1519  // Project::parse() is the primary entry point for calling the frontend
1520  // and generating the AST for all files found on the command line.
1521  //---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1522  errorCode = parse();
1523  set_frontendErrorCode(errorCode);
1524  }
1525 
1526  // DQ (8/22/2009): We test the parent of SgFunctionTypeTable in the AST post processing,
1527  // so we need to make sure that it is set.
1528  SgFunctionTypeTable* functionTypeTable = SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable();
1529  ASSERT_not_null(functionTypeTable);
1530  if (functionTypeTable->get_parent() == nullptr)
1531  {
1532  if (numberOfFiles() > 0)
1533  functionTypeTable->set_parent(&(get_file(0)));
1534  else
1535  functionTypeTable->set_parent(this);
1536  }
1537  ASSERT_not_null(functionTypeTable->get_parent());
1538  ASSERT_not_null(SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable());
1539  ASSERT_not_null(SgNode::get_globalFunctionTypeTable()->get_parent());
1540 
1541  // DQ (7/25/2010): We test the parent of SgTypeTable in the AST post processing,
1542  // so we need to make sure that it is set.
1543  SgTypeTable* typeTable = SgNode::get_globalTypeTable();
1544  ASSERT_not_null(typeTable);
1545  if (typeTable->get_parent() == nullptr)
1546  {
1547  if (numberOfFiles() > 0)
1548  typeTable->set_parent(&(get_file(0)));
1549  else
1550  typeTable->set_parent(this);
1551  }
1552  ASSERT_not_null(typeTable->get_parent());
1553 
1554  ASSERT_not_null(SgNode::get_globalTypeTable());
1555  ASSERT_not_null(SgNode::get_globalTypeTable()->get_parent());
1556 
1557  return errorCode;
1558  }

1617 int
1618 SgProject::parse()
1619  {
1620  // volatile used as a work around for warning: variable might be clobbered by 'longjmp' or 'vfork'
1621  volatile int errorCode = 0;
1622 
1623 #define DEBUG_PARSE 0
1624 
1625  // DQ (7/6/2005): Introduce tracking of performance of ROSE.
1626  TimingPerformance timer ("AST (SgProject::parse()):");
1627 
1628 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_FORTRAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
1629  // FMZ (5/29/2008)
1630  FortranModuleInfo::setCurrentProject(this);
1631  FortranModuleInfo::set_inputDirs(this );
1632 #endif
1633 
1634 #ifdef ROSE_EXPERIMENTAL_JOVIAL_ROSE_CONNECTION
1635  ModuleBuilderFactory::get_compool_builder().setCurrentProject(this);
1636  ModuleBuilderFactory::get_compool_builder().setInputDirs(this);
1637 #endif
1638 
1639  // The goal in this version of the code is to separate the construction of the SgFile objects
1640  // from the invocation of the frontend on each of the SgFile objects. In general this allows
1641  // the compilation to reference the other SgFile objects on an as needed basis as part of running
1642  // the frontend. This is important for the optimization of Java.
1643  std::vector<SgFile*> vectorOfFiles;
1644  for (string currentFileName : p_sourceFileNameList)
1645  {
1646  int nextErrorCode = 0;
1647 
1648  // Exclude other files from list in argc and argv
1649  vector<string> argv = get_originalCommandLineArgumentList();
1650  CommandlineProcessing::removeAllFileNamesExcept(argv,p_sourceFileNameList,currentFileName);
1651 
1652  SgFile* newFile = determineFileType(argv, nextErrorCode, this);
1653  ASSERT_not_null(newFile);
1654  ASSERT_not_null(newFile->get_startOfConstruct());
1655 
1656  ASSERT_not_null(isSgProject(newFile->get_parent()));
1657  ROSE_ASSERT(newFile->get_parent() == this);
1658 
1659  // This just adds the new file to the list of files stored internally (note: this sets the parent of the newFile).
1660  set_file(*newFile);
1661  ASSERT_not_null(newFile->get_parent());
1662 
1663  // This list of files will be iterated over in call to the frontend in the next loop.
1664  vectorOfFiles.push_back(newFile);
1665  }
1666 
1667  // Run the frontend on each file in this project
1668  errorCode = this->RunFrontend();
1669  if (errorCode > 3) {
1670  return errorCode;
1671  }
1672 
1673  // DQ (6/13/2013): Test the new function to lookup the SgFile from the name with full path.
1674  // This is a simple consistency test for that new function.
1675  for (size_t i = 0; i < vectorOfFiles.size(); i++)
1676  {
1677  string filename = vectorOfFiles[i]->get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
1678  SgFile* file = this->operator[](filename);
1679  ASSERT_not_null(file);
1680 
1681  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 0 )
1682  {
1683  printf ("Testing: map of filenames to SgFile IR nodes: filename = %s is mapped to SgFile = %p \n",filename.c_str(),vectorOfFiles[i]);
1684  }
1685 
1686  ROSE_ASSERT(file == vectorOfFiles[i]);
1687  }
1688 
1689  // GB (8/19/2009): Moved the AstPostProcessing call from
1690  // SgFile::callFrontEnd to this point. Thus, it is only called once for
1691  // the whole project rather than once per file. Repeated calls to
1692  // AstPostProcessing are slow due to repeated memory pool traversals. The
1693  // AstPostProcessing is only to be called if there are input files to run
1694  // it on, and they are meant to be used in some way other than just
1695  // calling the backend on them. (If only the backend is used, this was
1696  // never called by SgFile::callFrontEnd either.)
1697 #ifndef ROSE_USE_CLANG_FRONTEND
1698  if ( (get_fileList().empty() == false) && (get_useBackendOnly() == false) )
1699  {
1700  AstPostProcessing(this);
1701  }
1702 #endif
1703 
1704  // negara1 (06/23/2011): Collect information about the included files to support unparsing of those that are modified.
1705  // In the first step, get the include search paths, which will be used while attaching include preprocessing infos.
1706  // Proceed only if there are input files and they require header files unparsing.
1707  if (!get_fileList().empty() && (*get_fileList().begin())->get_unparseHeaderFiles())
1708  {
1709  if (SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1)
1710  {
1711  cout << endl << "***HEADER FILES ANALYSIS***" << endl << endl;
1712  }
1713  CompilerOutputParser compilerOutputParser(this);
1714  const pair<list<string>, list<string> >& includedFilesSearchPaths = compilerOutputParser.collectIncludedFilesSearchPaths();
1715  set_quotedIncludesSearchPaths(includedFilesSearchPaths.first);
1716  set_bracketedIncludesSearchPaths(includedFilesSearchPaths.second);
1717 
1718  if (SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1)
1719  {
1720  // DQ (11/7/2018): Output the list of quotedIncludesSearchPaths and bracketedIncludesSearchPaths include paths.
1721  CollectionHelper::printList(get_quotedIncludesSearchPaths(), "\nQuoted includes search paths:", "Path:");
1722  CollectionHelper::printList(get_bracketedIncludesSearchPaths(), "\nBracketed includes search paths:", "Path:");
1723  }
1724  }
1725 
1726  // GB (9/4/2009): Moved the secondary pass over source files (which
1727  // attaches the preprocessing information) to this point. This way, the
1728  // secondary pass over each file runs after all fixes have been done. This
1729  // is relevant where the AstPostProcessing mechanism must first mark nodes
1730  // to be output before preprocessing information is attached.
1731  SgFilePtrList & files = get_fileList();
1732 
1733  // volatile used as a work around for warning: variable might be clobbered by 'longjmp' or 'vfork'
1734  volatile bool unparse_using_tokens = false;
1735 
1736  for (SgFile* file : files)
1737  {
1738  ASSERT_not_null(file);
1739 
1740  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = isSgSourceFile(file);
1741  if (sourceFile != nullptr)
1742  {
1743  // DQ (4/25/2021): I think this should be a static bool data member.
1744  if (unparse_using_tokens == false)
1745  {
1746  unparse_using_tokens = sourceFile->get_unparse_tokens();
1747  }
1748  }
1749 
1750  if (KEEP_GOING_CAUGHT_FRONTEND_SECONDARY_PASS_SIGNAL)
1751  {
1752  std::cout
1753  << "[WARN] "
1754  << "Configured to keep going after catching a signal in "
1755  << "SgFile::secondaryPassOverSourceFile()"
1756  << std::endl;
1757 
1758  if (file != nullptr)
1759  {
1760  file->set_frontendErrorCode(100);
1761 
1762  int save_volatile_variable = errorCode;
1763  errorCode = std::max(100, save_volatile_variable);
1764  }
1765  else
1766  {
1767  std::cout
1768  << "[FATAL] "
1769  << "Unable to keep going due to an unrecoverable internal error"
1770  << std::endl;
1771  // Liao, 4/25/2017. one assertion failure may trigger other assertion failures. We still want to keep going.
1772  exit(1);
1773  }
1774  }
1775  else
1776  {
1777  if (file->get_disable_edg_backend() == false)
1778  {
1779  // DQ (8/19/2019): Divide this into two parts, for optimization of header file unparsing, optionally
1780  // support the main file collection of comments and CPP directives, and separately the header file
1781  // collection of comments and CPP directives.
1782  file->secondaryPassOverSourceFile();
1783  ROSE_ASSERT(file->get_header_file_unparsing_optimization() == false);
1784  }
1785  }
1786  }
1787 
1788  if (errorCode != 0)
1789  {
1790  return errorCode;
1791  }
1792 
1793  // negara1 (06/23/2011): Collect information about the included files to support unparsing of those that are modified.
1794  // In the second step (after preprocessing infos are already attached), collect the including files map.
1795  // Proceed only if there are input files and they require header files unparsing.
1796  if (!get_fileList().empty() && (*get_fileList().begin())->get_unparseHeaderFiles())
1797  {
1798  CompilerOutputParser compilerOutputParser(this);
1799  const map<string, set<string> >& includedFilesMap = compilerOutputParser.collectIncludedFilesMap();
1800 
1801  IncludingPreprocessingInfosCollector includingPreprocessingInfosCollector(this, includedFilesMap);
1802  const map<string, set<PreprocessingInfo*> >& includingPreprocessingInfosMap = includingPreprocessingInfosCollector.collect();
1803 
1804  set_includingPreprocessingInfosMap(includingPreprocessingInfosMap);
1805 
1806  if (SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1)
1807  {
1808  printf ("\nOutput info for unparse headers support: \n");
1809  CollectionHelper::printMapOfSets(includedFilesMap, "\nIncluded files map:", "File:", "Included file:");
1810  CollectionHelper::printMapOfSets(get_includingPreprocessingInfosMap(), "\nIncluding files map:", "File:", "Including file:");
1811  }
1812 
1813  // DQ (4/25/2021): Adding code to process header files when file->get_header_file_unparsing_optimization() == false.
1814  if (SgFile::get_header_file_unparsing_optimization() == false)
1815  {
1816  std::map<std::string, SgIncludeFile*>::iterator i = EDG_ROSE_Translation::edg_include_file_map.begin();
1817  while (i != EDG_ROSE_Translation::edg_include_file_map.end())
1818  {
1819  string filename = i->first;
1820  SgIncludeFile* include_file = i->second;
1821  if (include_file != nullptr)
1822  {
1823  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = include_file->get_source_file();
1824  if (sourceFile != nullptr)
1825  {
1826  if (sourceFile->get_unparse_tokens() == false && unparse_using_tokens == true)
1827  {
1828  sourceFile->set_unparse_tokens(true);
1829  }
1830  ROSE_ASSERT(sourceFile->get_unparse_tokens() == unparse_using_tokens);
1831 
1832  sourceFile->secondaryPassOverSourceFile();
1833  }
1834  }
1835 
1836  i++;
1837  }
1838  }
1839  }
1840 
1841  if ( get_verbose() > 0 )
1842  {
1843  // Report the error code if it is non-zero (but only in verbose mode)
1844  if (errorCode > 0)
1845  {
1846  printf ("Frontend Warnings only: errorCode = %d \n",errorCode);
1847  if (errorCode > 3)
1848  {
1849  printf ("Frontend Errors found: errorCode = %d \n",errorCode);
1850  }
1851  }
1852  }
1853 
1854  // warnings from EDG processing are OK but not errors
1855  ROSE_ASSERT (errorCode <= 3);
1856 
1857  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() >= 1 )
1858  {
1859  cout << "C++ source(s) parsed. AST generated." << endl;
1860  }
1861 
1862  if ( get_verbose() > 3 )
1863  {
1864  printf ("In SgProject::parse() (verbose mode ON): \n");
1865  display ("In SgProject::parse()");
1866  }
1867 
1868 #if DEBUG_PARSE
1869  printf ("@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ \n");
1870  printf ("Leaving SgProject::parse(): errorCode = %d \n",errorCode);
1871  printf ("@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ \n");
1872 #endif
1873 
1874  return errorCode;
1875  } // end parse(;

1879 //negara1 (07/29/2011)
1880 //The returned file path is not normalized.
1881 //TODO: Return the normalized path after the bug in ROSE is fixed. The bug manifests itself when the same header file is included in
1882 //multiple places using different paths. In such a case, ROSE treats the same file as different files and generates different IDs for them.
1883 string SgProject::findIncludedFile(PreprocessingInfo* preprocessingInfo) {
1884  IncludeDirective includeDirective(preprocessingInfo -> getString());
1885  const string& includedPath = includeDirective.getIncludedPath();
1886  if (FileHelper::isAbsolutePath(includedPath)) {
1887  //the path is absolute, so no need to search for the file
1888  if (FileHelper::fileExists(includedPath)) {
1889  return includedPath;
1890  }
1891  return ""; //file does not exist, so return an empty string
1892  }
1893  if (includeDirective.isQuotedInclude()) {
1894  //start looking from the current folder, then proceed with the quoted includes search paths
1895  //TODO: Consider the presence of -I- option, which disables looking in the current folder for quoted includes.
1896  string currentFolder = FileHelper::getParentFolder(preprocessingInfo -> get_file_info() -> get_filenameString());
1897  p_quotedIncludesSearchPaths.insert(p_quotedIncludesSearchPaths.begin(), currentFolder);
1898  string includedFilePath = FileHelper::getIncludedFilePath(p_quotedIncludesSearchPaths, includedPath);
1899  p_quotedIncludesSearchPaths.erase(p_quotedIncludesSearchPaths.begin()); //remove the previously inserted current folder (for other files it might be different)
1900  if (!includedFilePath.empty()) {
1901  return includedFilePath;
1902  }
1903  }
1904  //For bracketed includes and for not yet found quoted includes proceed with the bracketed includes search paths
1905  return FileHelper::getIncludedFilePath(p_bracketedIncludesSearchPaths, includedPath);
1906 }

1953 string
1954 SgFile::generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename( string sourceFilename )
1955  {
1956  // DQ (9/24/2013): We need this assertion to make sure we are not causing what might be strange errors in memory.
1957  ROSE_ASSERT(sourceFilename.empty() == false);
1958 
1959  // Note: for "foo.F90" the fileNameSuffix() returns "F90"
1960  string filenameExtension = StringUtility::fileNameSuffix(sourceFilename);
1961 
1962  // DQ (9/24/2013): We need this assertion to make sure we are not causing what might be strange errors in memory.
1963  ROSE_ASSERT(filenameExtension.empty() == false);
1964 
1965  string sourceFileNameWithoutExtension = StringUtility::stripFileSuffixFromFileName(sourceFilename);
1966 
1967  // DQ (9/24/2013): We need this assertion to make sure we are not causing what might be strange errors in memory.
1968  ROSE_ASSERT(sourceFileNameWithoutExtension.empty() == false);
1969 
1970  // We need to turn on the 5th bit to make the capital a lower case character (assume ASCII)
1971  filenameExtension[0] = filenameExtension[0] | (1 << 5);
1972 
1973  // Rename the CPP generated intermediate file (strip path to put it in the current directory)
1974  string sourceFileNameWithoutPathAndWithoutExtension = StringUtility::stripPathFromFileName(sourceFileNameWithoutExtension);
1975  string sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp = sourceFileNameWithoutPathAndWithoutExtension + "_postprocessed." + filenameExtension;
1976 
1977  return sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp;
1978  }

1999 int
2000 SgFile::callFrontEnd()
2001  {
2002  // This function processes the command line and calls the EDG frontend.
2003  int frontendErrorLevel = 0;
2004  int fileNameIndex = 0;
2005 
2006  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0)
2007  {
2008  std::cout << "[INFO] [SgFile::callFrontEnd]" << std::endl;
2009  }
2010 
2011  TimingPerformance timer ("AST Front End Processing (SgFile):");
2012 
2013  // Build an argc,argv based C style commandline (we might not really need this)
2014  vector<string> argv = get_originalCommandLineArgumentList();
2015 
2016 #if ROSE_INTERNAL_DEBUG
2017  if (ROSE_DEBUG > 9)
2018  {
2019  // Print out the input arguments, so we can set them up internally instead of
2020  // on the command line (which is driving me nuts)
2021  for (unsigned int i=0; i < argv.size(); i++)
2022  printf ("argv[%d] = %s \n",i,argv[i]);
2023  }
2024 #endif
2025 
2026  // Save this so that it can be used in the template instantiation phase later.
2027  // This file is later written into the *.ti file so that the compilation can
2028  // be repeated as required to instantiate all function templates.
2029  std::string translatorCommandLineString = CommandlineProcessing::generateStringFromArgList(argv,false,true);
2030  set_savedFrontendCommandLine(translatorCommandLineString);
2031 
2032  // local copies of argc and argv variables
2033  // The purpose of building local copies is to avoid
2034  // the modification of the command line by SLA
2035  vector<string> localCopy_argv = argv;
2036 
2037  // Process command line options specific to ROSE
2038  // This leaves all filenames and non-rose specific option in the argv list
2039  processRoseCommandLineOptions (localCopy_argv);
2040 
2041  // DQ (6/21/2005): Process template specific options so that we can generated
2042  // code for the backend compiler (this processing is backend specific).
2043  processBackendSpecificCommandLineOptions (localCopy_argv);
2044 
2045  vector<string> inputCommandLine;
2046 
2047  // Build the commandline for EDG
2048  if (get_C_only() || get_Cxx_only() || get_Cuda_only() || get_OpenCL_only() )
2049  {
2050 #ifdef BACKEND_CXX_IS_CLANG_COMPILER
2051  #if ((ROSE_EDG_MAJOR_VERSION_NUMBER == 4) && (ROSE_EDG_MINOR_VERSION_NUMBER >= 9) ) || (ROSE_EDG_MAJOR_VERSION_NUMBER > 4)
2052  // OK, we are supporting Clang using EDG 4.9 and greater.
2053  #else
2054  printf ("\nERROR: Clang compiler as backend to ROSE is not supported unless using EDG 4.9 version \n");
2055  printf (" or greater (use --enable-edg_version=4.9 or greater to configure ROSE). \n\n");
2056  exit(1);
2057  #endif
2058 #endif
2059 
2060 #ifndef ROSE_USE_CLANG_FRONTEND
2061  build_EDG_CommandLine (inputCommandLine,localCopy_argv,fileNameIndex );
2062 #else
2063  build_CLANG_CommandLine (inputCommandLine,localCopy_argv,fileNameIndex );
2064 #endif
2065  }
2066 
2067  std::string tmp_translatorCommandLineString = CommandlineProcessing::generateStringFromArgList(inputCommandLine,false,true);
2068 
2069  // Exit if we are to ONLY call the vendor's backend compiler
2070  if (p_useBackendOnly == true)
2071  {
2072  return 0;
2073  }
2074 
2075  ROSE_ASSERT (p_useBackendOnly == false);
2076 
2077  if ((get_C_only() || get_Cxx_only()) &&
2078  get_disable_edg_backend() == false && get_new_frontend() == true)
2079  {
2080  printf ("Rose::new_frontend == true (call edgFrontEnd using unix system() function!) \n");
2081 
2082  std::string frontEndCommandLineString;
2083  if ( get_KCC_frontend() == true )
2084  {
2085  frontEndCommandLineString = "KCC "; // -cpfe_only is no longer supported (I think)
2086  }
2087  else
2088  {
2089  frontEndCommandLineString = "edgcpfe --g++ --gnu_version 40201 ";
2090  }
2091  frontEndCommandLineString += CommandlineProcessing::generateStringFromArgList(inputCommandLine,true,false);
2092 
2093  if ( get_verbose() > -1 )
2094  printf ("frontEndCommandLineString = %s \n\n",frontEndCommandLineString.c_str());
2095 
2096  int status = system(frontEndCommandLineString.c_str());
2097 
2098  printf ("After calling edgcpfe as a test (status = %d) \n",status);
2099  ROSE_ASSERT(status == 0);
2100  }
2101  else
2102  {
2103  if ((get_C_only() || get_Cxx_only()) && get_disable_edg_backend() == true)
2104  {
2105  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0)
2106  {
2107  std::cout << "[INFO] [SgFile::callFrontEnd] Skipping EDG frontend" << std::endl;
2108  }
2109  }
2110  else
2111  {
2112  switch (this->variantT())
2113  {
2114  case V_SgFile:
2115  case V_SgSourceFile:
2116  {
2117  SgSourceFile* sourceFile = const_cast<SgSourceFile*>(isSgSourceFile(this));
2118  ASSERT_not_null(sourceFile);
2119  frontendErrorLevel = sourceFile->buildAST(localCopy_argv, inputCommandLine);
2120  break;
2121  }
2122 
2123 #ifdef ROSE_ENABLE_BINARY_ANALYSIS
2124  case V_SgBinaryComposite:
2125  {
2126  SgBinaryComposite* binary = const_cast<SgBinaryComposite*>(isSgBinaryComposite(this));
2127  ASSERT_not_null(binary);
2128  frontendErrorLevel = binary->buildAST(localCopy_argv, inputCommandLine);
2129  break;
2130  }
2131 #endif
2132 
2133  case V_SgUnknownFile:
2134  {
2135  break;
2136  }
2137 
2138  default:
2139  {
2140  printf ("Error: default reached in Rose parser/IR translation processing: class name = %s \n",this->class_name().c_str());
2141  ROSE_ABORT();
2142  }
2143  }
2144  }
2145  }
2146 
2147  // if there are warnings report that there are in the verbose mode and continue
2148  if (frontendErrorLevel > 0)
2149  {
2150  if ( get_verbose() >= 1 )
2151  cout << "Warnings in Rose parser/IR translation processing! (continuing ...) " << endl;
2152  }
2153 
2154 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_FORTRAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
2155  // FMZ: 05/30/2008. Do not generate .rmod file for the PU imported by "use" stmt
2156  // DXN (01/18/2011): Fixed to build rmod file only when there is no error passed back from the frontend.
2157  if (get_Fortran_only() == true && FortranModuleInfo::isRmodFile() == false && frontendErrorLevel == 0)
2158  {
2159  if (get_verbose() > 1)
2160  printf ("Generating a Fortran 90 module file (*.rmod) \n");
2161 
2162  generateModFile(this);
2163 
2164  if (get_verbose() > 1)
2165  printf ("DONE: Generating a Fortran 90 module file (*.rmod) \n");
2166  }
2167 #endif
2168 
2169  return frontendErrorLevel;
2170  }

2266  // **************************************************************************
2267  // Secondary Pass Over Source File
2268  // **************************************************************************
2269  // This pass collects extra information about the source file that may not have
2270  // been available from previous tools that operated on the file. For example:
2271  // 1) EDG ignores comments and so we collect the whole token stream in this phase.
2272  // 2) OFP ignores comments similarly to EDG and so we collect the whole token stream.
2273  // 3) Binary disassembly ignores the binary format so we collect this information
2274  // about the structure of the ELF binary separately.
2275  // For source code (C,C++,Fortran) we collect the whole token stream, for example:
2276  // 1) Comments
2277  // 2) Preprocessors directives
2278  // 3) White space
2279  // 4) All tokens (each is classified as to what specific type of token it is)
2280  //
2281  // There is no secondary processing for binaries.
2282 
2283  // DQ (10/27/2018): Added documentation.

2505 void
2506 SgSourceFile_processCppLinemarkers::FixupASTSourcePositionsBasedOnDetectedLineDirectives::visit ( SgNode* astNode )
2507  {
2508  // DQ (12/14/2012): This functionality is being added to support applications like sudo which have generated code from tools like lex.
2509  // This traversal is defined to detect the use of "#line" directived and then accumulate the list of filenames used in the #line directives.
2510  // When #line directives are used in the input source file then we consider all statements associated with those filenames to be from the
2511  // input source file and direct them to be unparsed. The actual way we trigger them to be unparsed is to make the source position to
2512  // be unparsed in the Sg_File_Info object, this is enough to force the unparsed to output those statements.
2513  // TODO: It might be that this should operate on SgLocatedNode IR nodes instead of SgStatement IR nodes.
2514 
2515  SgStatement* statement = isSgStatement(astNode);
2516 
2517  if (statement != nullptr)
2518  {
2519  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
2520  printf ("FixupASTSourcePositionsBasedOnDetectedLineDirectives::visit(): statement = %p = %s \n",statement,statement->class_name().c_str());
2521 
2522  ASSERT_not_null(statement->get_file_info());
2523  int fileId = statement->get_file_info()->get_file_id();
2524 
2525  // Check if this fileId is associated with set of fileId that we would like to output.
2526  if (filenameIdList.find(fileId) != filenameIdList.end())
2527  {
2528  statement->get_startOfConstruct()->setOutputInCodeGeneration();
2529  statement->get_endOfConstruct() ->setOutputInCodeGeneration();
2530  }
2531  }
2532  }

3233  SgSourceFile* fortranSourceFile = const_cast<SgSourceFile*>(this);
3234  frontendErrorLevel = experimental_fortran_main (experimental_FortranParser_argc,
3235  experimental_FortranParser_argv,
3236  fortranSourceFile);
3237 #else
3238  printf ("ROSE_EXPERIMENTAL_FLANG_ROSE_CONNECTION is not defined \n");
3239 #endif
3240 
3241  if (frontendErrorLevel == 0)
3242  {
3243  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 ) mlog[INFO] << "SUCCESS with call to experimental_FortranParser_main()\n";
3244  }
3245  else
3246  {
3247  mlog[FATAL] << "Error returned from call to experimental_FortranParser_main(): frontendErrorLevel = "
3248  << frontendErrorLevel << "\n";
3249  ROSE_ABORT();
3250  }
3251  }
3252  else
3253  {
3254  frontendErrorLevel = openFortranParser_main (openFortranParser_argc, openFortranParser_argv);
3255  }
3256 
3257 
3258  // DQ (11/11/2010): There should be no include files left in the stack, see test2010_78.C and test2010_79.C when
3259  // compiled together on the same command line.
3260  if (astIncludeStack.size() != 0)
3261  {
3262  mprintf ("Warning: astIncludeStack not cleaned up after openFortranParser_main(): astIncludeStack.size() = %" PRIuPTR " \n",astIncludeStack.size());
3263  }
3264 #endif
3265 
3266  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
3267  printf ("DONE: Calling the openFortranParser_main() function (which loads the JVM) \n");
3268 
3269  // Reset this global pointer after we are done (just to be safe and avoid it being used later and causing strange bugs).
3270  OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer = nullptr;
3271 
3272  // Now read the CPP directives such as "# <number> <filename> <optional numeric code>", in the generated file from CPP.
3273  if (requires_C_preprocessor == true)
3274  {
3275  // If this was part of the processing of a CPP generated file then read the preprocessed file
3276  // to get the CPP directives (different from those of the original *.F?? file) which will
3277  // indicate line numbers and files where text was inserted as part of CPP processing. We
3278  // mostly want to read CPP declarations of the form "# <number> <filename> <optional numeric code>".
3279  // these are the only directives that will be in the CPP generated file (as I recall).
3280 
3281  string sourceFilename = get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
3282  string sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp = generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename(sourceFilename);
3283 #if 0
3284  printf ("Need to preprocess the CPP generated fortran file so that we can attribute source code statements to files: sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp = %s \n",sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp.c_str());
3285 #endif
3286 #if 1
3287  // Note that the collection of CPP linemarker directives from the CPP generated file
3288  // (and their insertion into the AST), should be done before the collection and
3289  // insertion of the Comments and more general CPP directives from the original source
3290  // file and their insertion. This will allow the correct representation of source
3291  // position information to be used in the final insertion of comments and CPP directives
3292  // from the original file.
3293 
3294  attachPreprocessingInfo(this);
3295 
3296  // DQ (12/19/2008): Now we have to do an analysis of the AST to interpret the linemarkers.
3297  processCppLinemarkers();
3298 
3299 #endif
3300  }
3301 
3302  // printf ("######################### Leaving SgSourceFile::build_Fortran_AST() ############################ \n");
3303 
3304 
3305  // DQ (10/26/2010): Moved from SgSourceFile::callFrontEnd() so that the stack will
3306  // be empty when processing Java language support (not Fortran).
3307  delete currStks;
3308  currStks = nullptr;
3309 
3310  return frontendErrorLevel;
3311 #else
3312  fprintf(stderr, "Fortran parser not supported \n");
3313  ROSE_ABORT();
3314 #endif
3315  }

3340 int
3341 Rose::Frontend::RunSerial(SgProject* project)
3342 {
3343  // volatile used as a work around for warning: variable might be clobbered by 'longjmp' or 'vfork'
3344  volatile int status_of_function = 0;
3345 
3346  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0) {
3347  mlog[INFO] << "[Frontend] Running in serial mode\n";
3348  }
3349 
3350  std::vector<SgFile*> all_files = project->get_fileList();
3351  {
3352  int status_of_file = 0;
3353  for (SgFile* file : all_files)
3354  {
3355  ASSERT_not_null(file);
3356  if (KEEP_GOING_CAUGHT_FRONTEND_SIGNAL)
3357  {
3358  std::cout
3359  << "[WARN] "
3360  << "Configured to keep going after catching a "
3361  << "signal in SgFile::RunFrontend()"
3362  << std::endl;
3363 
3364  if (file != nullptr)
3365  {
3366  int save_volatile_variable = status_of_function;
3367  file->set_frontendErrorCode(100);
3368  status_of_function = std::max(100, save_volatile_variable);
3369  }
3370  else
3371  {
3372  std::cout
3373  << "[FATAL] "
3374  << "Unable to keep going due to an unrecoverable internal error"
3375  << std::endl;
3376  exit(1);
3377  }
3378  }
3379  else
3380  {
3381  //-----------------------------------------------------------
3382  // Pass File to Frontend. Avoid using try/catch/re-throw if not necessary because it interferes with debugging
3383  // the exception (it makes it hard to find where the exception was originally thrown). Also, no need to print a
3384  // fatal message to std::cout(!) if the exception inherits from the STL properly since the C++ runtime will do
3385  // all that for us. [Robb P. Matzke 2015-01-07]
3386  //-----------------------------------------------------------
3387  if (Rose::KeepGoing::g_keep_going) {
3388  try {
3389  int save_volatile_variable = status_of_function;
3390  file->runFrontend(status_of_file); // status_of_file is modified as a side effect
3391  status_of_function = max(status_of_file, save_volatile_variable);
3392  } catch (...) {
3393  if (file != nullptr) {
3394  file->set_frontendErrorCode(100);
3395  } else {
3396  std::cout
3397  << "[FATAL] "
3398  << "Unable to keep going due to an unrecoverable internal error"
3399  << std::endl;
3400  exit(1);
3401  }
3402  raise(SIGABRT); // catch with signal handling above
3403  }
3404  } else {
3405  // Same thing but without the try/catch because we want the exception to be propagated all the way to the
3406  // user without us re-throwing it and interfering with debugging.
3407  int save_volatile_variable = status_of_function;
3408  file->runFrontend(status_of_file); // status_of_file is modified as a side effect
3409  status_of_function = max(status_of_file, save_volatile_variable);
3410  }
3411  }
3412  }
3413  } //all_files->callFrontEnd
3414 
3415  ASSERT_not_null(project);
3416 
3417  project->set_frontendErrorCode(status_of_function);
3418 
3419  return status_of_function;
3420 } // Rose::Frontend::RunSerial

3452 Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::RunBatchMode(SgProject* project)

3456 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
3457  namespace ecj = Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj;
3458 
3459  {
3460  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)

3463  // Setup global pointer to this project to be

3479  // This leaves all filenames and non-rose specific option in the

3495 
3496  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 1)
3497  {
3498  std::string cmdline_string = boost::algorithm::join(cmdline, " ");
3499  std::cout << "[INFO] [Frontend] [Java] ECJ commandline: " << cmdline_string << std::endl;
3500  }
3501 
3502  status = openJavaParser_main(argc, argv);
3503  {
3504  project->set_ecjErrorCode(status);
3505  }
3506  }
3507  }
3508 #else
3509  // DQ (2/21/2016): Added "error: " to allow this to be caught by the ROSE Matrix Testing.
3511  ROSE_ASSERT (! "[FATAL] [ROSE] [frontend] [Java] error: ROSE was not configured to support the Java frontend, see ROSE/configure --help.");
3512 #endif
3513 
3514  return status;
