3633 
3634 
3635 int
3636 SgSourceFile::build_Java_AST( vector<string> argv, vector<string> inputCommandLine )
3637  {
3638  if (this -> get_package() != nullptr || this -> attributeExists("error")) { // Has this file been processed already? If so, ignore it.
3639  return 0;
3640  }
3641 
3642  // SG (7/9/2015) In case of a mixed language project, force case
3643  // sensitivity here.
3644  SageBuilder::symbol_table_case_insensitive_semantics = false;
3645 
3646 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
3647  ROSE_ASSERT(get_requires_C_preprocessor() == false);
3648 
3649  SgProject* project = this->get_project();
3650 
3651  std::string classpath = Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::GetClasspath(project);
3652  std::string sourcepath = Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::GetSourcepath(project);
3653  std::string source_version = Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::GetSourceVersion(project);
3654  std::string target_version = Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::GetTargetVersion(project);
3655 
3656  // *******************************************************
3657  // Build syntax checking command line call
3658  // *******************************************************
3659 
3660  // DQ (9/19/2011): This is what I thought, but it does not appear to be true or we tie into ECJ at the
3661  // the wrong location so that we don't get any syntax checking. So we need to introduce a pass using
3662  // the backend compiler to support the syntax checking for Java.
3663  // DQ (10/11/2010): We don't need syntax checking because ECJ will do that.
3664  bool syntaxCheckInputCode = (get_skip_syntax_check() == false);
3665  if (syntaxCheckInputCode == true)
3666  {
3667  // Introduce tracking of performance of ROSE.
3668  TimingPerformance timer ("Java syntax checking of input:");
3669 
3670  // DQ (9/19/2011): For Java we want to run the backend javacc compiler to do the syntax checking.
3671  string backendJavaCompiler = BACKEND_JAVA_COMPILER_NAME_WITH_PATH;
3672  if ( get_verbose() > 2 )
3673  {
3674  printf ("@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ Setting up Java Syntax check @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ \n");
3675  printf ("BACKEND_JAVA_COMPILER_NAME_WITH_PATH = %s \n",backendJavaCompiler.c_str());
3676  }
3677  // Start building the javac command line
3678  vector<string> javaCommandLine;
3679  javaCommandLine.push_back(backendJavaCompiler);
3680 
3681  // DQ (7/20/2011):Each part of the option for "-sourcepath <path>" or "-d <path>"
3682  // must be pushed onto the javaCommandLine separately.
3683  if ( get_verbose() > 2 )
3684  javaCommandLine.push_back("-verbose");
3685 
3686  // Always push the source information
3687  javaCommandLine.push_back("-source");
3688  {
3689  if (source_version.size() > 0) {
3690  javaCommandLine.push_back(source_version);
3691  } else /* default */ {
3692  javaCommandLine.push_back("1.6");
3693  }
3694  }
3695 
3696  // We invoke javac to check the syntax of the input program
3697  // Since it doesn generates classes, we create a separate folder
3698  // just to make sure this gets contained somewhere.
3699  string backendClassOutput = "javac-syntax-check-classes";
3700  javaCommandLine.push_back("-d");
3701  javaCommandLine.push_back(backendClassOutput);
3702  boost::filesystem::create_directory(backendClassOutput.c_str());
3703  if (!boost::filesystem::exists(backendClassOutput.c_str())) {
3704  printf ("Can't create destination folder for syntax checking\n");
3705  ROSE_ABORT();
3706  }
3707 
3708  if (classpath.size()) {
3709  javaCommandLine.push_back("-classpath");
3710  javaCommandLine.push_back(classpath);
3711  }
3712 
3713  if (sourcepath.size()) {
3714  javaCommandLine.push_back("-sourcepath");
3715  javaCommandLine.push_back(sourcepath);
3716  }
3717 
3718  // Specify warnings for javac compiler.
3719  if (backendJavaCompiler == "javac" || backendJavaCompiler == "javac.exe") {
3720  if (get_output_warnings() == true) {
3721  javaCommandLine.push_back("-Xlint");
3722  } else {
3723  javaCommandLine.push_back("-Xlint:none");
3724  }
3725  javaCommandLine.push_back("-proc:none");
3726  }
3727  else
3728  {
3729  printf ("Currently only the javac compiler backend is supported backendCompilerSystem = %s \n",backendJavaCompiler.c_str());
3730  ROSE_ABORT();
3731  }
3732 
3733  javaCommandLine.push_back(get_sourceFileNameWithPath());
3734 
3735  // At this point we have the full command line with the source file name
3736  if (get_verbose() > 1)
3737  {
3738  printf ("Checking syntax of input program using javac: syntaxCheckingCommandline = %s \n",CommandlineProcessing::generateStringFromArgList(javaCommandLine,false,false).c_str());
3739  }
3740 
3741  int returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler = 0;
3742  // Call the OS with the commandline defined by: syntaxCheckingCommandline
3743  returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler = systemFromVector (javaCommandLine);
3744 
3745  // Check that there are no errors, I think that warnings are ignored!
3746  if (returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler != 0)
3747  {
3748  printf ("Syntax errors detected in input java program ... status = %d \n",returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler);
3749 
3750 // TODO: Remove this! PC 07/03/2013
3751 // // We should define some convention for error codes returned by ROSE
3752 // throw std::exception();
3753  return returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler;
3754  }
3755 // TODO: Remove this! PC 07/03/2013
3756 // ROSE_ASSERT(returnValueForSyntaxCheckUsingBackendCompiler == 0);
3757 
3758  if ( get_verbose() > 2 )
3759  {
3760  printf ("@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ DONE: Setting up Java Syntax check @@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@ \n");
3761  }
3762  }
3763 
3764  // *******************************************************
3765  if (get_output_parser_actions() == true)
3766  {
3767  printf("Sorry, not implemented: output_parser_actions option is not supported for Java yet. \n");
3768  ROSE_ABORT();
3769  }
3770 
3771  // Option to just run the parser (not constructing the AST) and quit.
3772  if (get_exit_after_parser() == true)
3773  {
3774  printf("Sorry, not implemented: get_exit_after_parser option is not supported for Java yet. \n");
3775  ROSE_ABORT();
3776  }
3777 
3778  // *******************************************************
3779  // Build the call to the ECJ frontend
3780  // *******************************************************
3781 
3782  // Note that for the ECJ JVM support, the filename must appear last on the command line.
3783  // I think it is only an intermediate test before actually calling ECJ that requires
3784  // this so it could be relaxed with a bit of work.
3785  vector<string> frontEndCommandLine;
3786  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(argv[0]);
3787 
3788  // Added an option to the ECJ command line to support different levels of output from the Java side of the house.
3789  string verboseOptionString = "-rose:verbose " + StringUtility::numberToString(SgProject::get_verbose());
3790  if (SgProject::get_verbose() > 0)
3791  {
3792  printf ("Debugging option to Java ECJ translation (java code) to build ROSE AST: verboseOptionString = %s \n",verboseOptionString.c_str());
3793  }
3794  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(verboseOptionString);
3795 
3796  // *******************************************************************
3797  // Handle java rose options we need to transmit to ecj
3798  // !! Warning !! ECJ does not accept '--' prefixed options.
3799  // *******************************************************************
3800  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-source");
3801  if (source_version.size() > 0) {
3802  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(source_version);
3803  } else /* default */ {
3804  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("1.6");
3805  }
3806 
3807  if (target_version.size() > 0) {
3808  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-target");
3809  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(target_version);
3810  }
3811 
3812  if (!get_output_warnings()) {
3813  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-nowarn");
3814  }
3815 
3816 // TODO: Remove this !
3817 /*
3818  // This is to specify where ecj should output the .class it is temporarily generating.
3819  // Check if -decj has already been provided, if not default to a unique name consisting
3820  // of the prefix "ecj-classes" with the suffix "-" + source_file_name, where source_file_name
3821  // is the simple name of the input source file without the ".java" suffix.
3822  string ecjDestDir;
3823  if (!CommandlineProcessing::isOptionWithParameter(javaRoseOptionList, "", "decj", ecjDestDir, false)) {
3824  string full_file_name = get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
3825  int last_slash = full_file_name.find_last_of("/\\");
3826  string file_name = full_file_name.substr(last_slash + 1);
3827  int dot = file_name.find_last_of(".");
3828  if (dot != -1) {
3829  file_name = file_name.substr(0, dot);
3830  }
3831 
3832  ecjDestDir = "ecj-classes-" + file_name + "/";
3833  }
3834  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-d");
3835  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(ecjDestDir);
3836 
3837  // Setup the classpath and append the classes folder ecj outputs its temporary files to
3838  // Note: it is important to append since we do not want to override any user provided paths
3839  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-classpath");
3840  frontEndCommandLine.push_back((classpath.size() > 0 ? (classpath + ":") : "") + ecjDestDir);
3841 */
3842 
3843  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-d");
3844  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("none");
3845  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-classpath");
3846  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(classpath);
3847 
3848  if (sourcepath.size()) {
3849  frontEndCommandLine.push_back("-sourcepath");
3850  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(sourcepath);
3851  }
3852 
3853  // Java does not use include files, so we can enforce this.
3854  ROSE_ASSERT(get_project()->get_includeDirectorySpecifierList().empty() == true);
3855 
3856  // Add the source file as the last argument on the command line (checked by intermediate testing before calling ECJ).
3857  frontEndCommandLine.push_back(get_sourceFileNameWithPath());
3858 
3859  if ( get_verbose() > 0 )
3860  printf ("Java numberOfCommandLineArguments = %" PRIuPTR " frontEndCommandLine = %s \n",inputCommandLine.size(),CommandlineProcessing::generateStringFromArgList(frontEndCommandLine,false,false).c_str());
3861 
3862  int ecjArgc = 0;
3863  char** ecjArgv = nullptr;
3864  CommandlineProcessing::generateArgcArgvFromList(frontEndCommandLine,ecjArgc,ecjArgv);
3865 
3866  // ECJ AST will attach to this project's shared global scope [TOO1, 2014-04-02]
3867  Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::Ecj_globalProjectPointer = this->get_project();
3868  ASSERT_not_null(Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::Ecj_globalProjectPointer);
3869 
3870 #if USE_ROSE_SSL_SUPPORT
3871  // The use of the JVM required to support Java is a problem when linking to the SSL library (either -lssl or -lcrypto)
3872  // this may be fixed in Java version 6, but this is a hope, it has not been tested. Java version 6 does
3873  // appear to fix the problem with zlib (we think) and this appears to be a similar problem).
3874  int frontendErrorLevel = 1;
3875  printf ("********************************************************************************************** \n");
3876  printf ("Java support using the JVM is incompatable with the use of the SSL library (fails in jvm). \n");
3877  printf ("To enable the use of Java support in ROSE don't use --enable-ssl on configure command line. \n");
3878  printf ("********************************************************************************************** \n");
3879 #else
3880  int frontendErrorLevel = openJavaParser_main (ecjArgc, ecjArgv);
3881 #endif
3882 
3883  if ( get_verbose() > 0 )
3884  printf ("DONE: Calling the openFortranParser_main() function (which loads the JVM) \n");
3885 
3886  // Reset this global pointer after we are done (just to be safe and avoid it being used later and causing strange bugs).
3887  Rose::Frontend::Java::Ecj::Ecj_globalProjectPointer = nullptr;
3888 
3889  return frontendErrorLevel;
3890 #else
3891  fprintf(stderr, "Java language parser not supported \n");
3892  ROSE_ABORT();
3893 #endif
3894  }

3896 namespace SgSourceFile_processCppLinemarkers
3897  {
3898  // This class (AST traversal) supports the traversal of the AST required
3899  // to translate the source position using the CPP linemarkers.
3900 
3901  class LinemarkerTraversal : public AstSimpleProcessing
3902  {
3903  public:
3904  // list<PreprocessingInfo*> preprocessingInfoStack;
3905  list< pair<int,int> > sourcePositionStack;
3906 
3907  LinemarkerTraversal( const string & sourceFilename );
3908 
3909  void visit ( SgNode* astNode );
3910  };
3911  }

3913 
3914 SgSourceFile_processCppLinemarkers::LinemarkerTraversal::LinemarkerTraversal( const string & sourceFilename )
3915  {
3916  // Build an initial element on the stack so that the original source file name will be used to
3917  // set the global scope (which will be traversed before we visit any statements that might have
3918  // CPP directives attached (or which are CPP direcitve IR nodes).
3919 
3920  // Get the fileId of the assocated filename
3921  int fileId = Sg_File_Info::getIDFromFilename(sourceFilename);
3922 
3923  // Assume this is line 1 (I forget why zero is not a great idea here,
3924  // I expect that it causes a consstancy test to fail somewhere).
3925  int line = 1;
3926 
3927  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
3928  printf ("In LinemarkerTraversal::LinemarkerTraversal(): Push initial stack entry for line = %d fileId = %d sourceFilename = %s \n",line,fileId,sourceFilename.c_str());
3929 
3930  // Push an entry onto the stack before doing the traversal over the whole AST.
3931  sourcePositionStack.push_front( pair<int,int>(line,fileId) );
3932  }

3939 void
3940 SgSourceFile_processCppLinemarkers::LinemarkerTraversal::visit ( SgNode* astNode )
3941  {
3942 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_FORTRAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
3943 
3944  // DXN (02/21/2011): Consider the case of SgInterfaceBody.
3945  // TODO: revise SgInterfaceBody::get_numberOfTraversalSuccessor() to return 1 and
3946  // TODO: revise SgInterfaceBody::get_traversalSuccessorByIndex(int ) to return p_functionDeclaration
3947  // Such changes will require some re-write of the code to build SgInterfaceBody.
3948  // With such changes, the patch below to treat the case of SgInterfaceBody will no longer be necessary.
3949  SgInterfaceBody* interfaceBody = isSgInterfaceBody(astNode);
3950  if (interfaceBody)
3951  {
3952  AstSimpleProcessing::traverse(interfaceBody->get_functionDeclaration(), preorder);
3953  }
3954 
3955  SgStatement* statement = isSgStatement(astNode);
3956  // printf ("LinemarkerTraversal::visit(): statement = %p = %s \n",statement,(statement != nullptr) ? statement->class_name().c_str() : "NULL");
3957  if (statement != nullptr)
3958  {
3959  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
3960  printf ("LinemarkerTraversal::visit(): statement = %p = %s \n",statement,statement->class_name().c_str());
3961 
3962  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType *commentOrDirectiveList = statement->getAttachedPreprocessingInfo();
3963 
3964  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
3965  printf ("LinemarkerTraversal::visit(): commentOrDirectiveList = %p (size = %" PRIuPTR ") \n",commentOrDirectiveList,(commentOrDirectiveList != NULL) ? commentOrDirectiveList->size() : 0);
3966 
3967  if (commentOrDirectiveList != nullptr)
3968  {
3969  AttachedPreprocessingInfoType::iterator i = commentOrDirectiveList->begin();
3970  while(i != commentOrDirectiveList->end())
3971  {
3972  if ( (*i)->getTypeOfDirective() == PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorCompilerGeneratedLinemarker )
3973  {
3974  // This is a CPP linemarker
3975  int line = (*i)->get_lineNumberForCompilerGeneratedLinemarker();
3976 
3977  // DQ (12/23/2008): Note this is a quoted name, we need the unquoted version!
3978  std::string quotedFilename = (*i)->get_filenameForCompilerGeneratedLinemarker();
3979  ROSE_ASSERT(quotedFilename[0] == '\"');
3980  ROSE_ASSERT(quotedFilename[quotedFilename.length()-1] == '\"');
3981  std::string filename = quotedFilename.substr(1,quotedFilename.length()-2);
3982 
3983  std::string options = (*i)->get_optionalflagsForCompilerGeneratedLinemarker();
3984 
3985  // Add the new filename to the static map stored in the Sg_File_Info (no action if filename is already in the map).
3986  Sg_File_Info::addFilenameToMap(filename);
3987 
3988  int fileId = Sg_File_Info::getIDFromFilename(filename);
3989 
3990  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
3991  printf ("line = %d fileId = %d quotedFilename = %s filename = %s options = %s \n",line,fileId,quotedFilename.c_str(),filename.c_str(),options.c_str());
3992 
3993  // Just record the first linemarker so that we can test getting the filename correct.
3994  if (line == 1 && sourcePositionStack.empty() == true)
3995  {
3996  sourcePositionStack.push_front( pair<int,int>(line,fileId) );
3997  }
3998  }
3999 
4000  i++;
4001  }
4002  }
4003 
4004  // ROSE_ASSERT(sourcePositionStack.empty() == false);
4005  if (sourcePositionStack.empty() == false)
4006  {
4007  int line = sourcePositionStack.front().first;
4008  int fileId = sourcePositionStack.front().second;
4009 
4010  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
4011  printf ("Setting the source position of statement = %p = %s to line = %d fileId = %d \n",statement,statement->class_name().c_str(),line,fileId);
4012 
4013  // DXN (02/18/2011): only reset the file id for the node whose file id corresponds to the "_postprocessed" file.
4014  string sourceFilename = Sg_File_Info::getFilenameFromID(fileId) ;
4015  string sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp = OpenFortranParser_globalFilePointer->generate_C_preprocessor_intermediate_filename(sourceFilename);
4016  int cppFileId = Sg_File_Info::getIDFromFilename(sourceFileNameOutputFromCpp);
4017  if (statement->get_file_info()->get_file_id() == cppFileId)
4018  {
4019  statement->get_file_info()->set_file_id(fileId);
4020  }
4021  // statement->get_file_info()->set_line(line);
4022 
4023  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
4024  Sg_File_Info::display_static_data("Setting the source position of statement");
4025 
4026  string filename = Sg_File_Info::getFilenameFromID(fileId);
4027 
4028  if ( SgProject::get_verbose() > 1 )
4029  {
4030  printf ("filename = %s \n",filename.c_str());
4031  printf ("filename = %s \n",statement->get_file_info()->get_filenameString().c_str());
4032  }
4033 
4034  ASSERT_not_null(statement->get_file_info()->get_filename());
4035  ROSE_ASSERT(statement->get_file_info()->get_filenameString().empty() == false);
4036  }
4037  }
4038 #else // ! ROSE_BUILD_FORTRAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
4039  // SKW: not called except from Fortran
4040  printf(">>> SgSourceFile_processCppLinemarkers::LinemarkerTraversal::visit is not implemented for languages other than Fortran\n");
4041  ROSE_ABORT();
4042 #endif // ROSE_BUILD_FORTRAN_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
4043  }

4252  {

4255  // DXN (01/10/2011): except for building C and Cxx AST, frontend fails when frontend error level > 0.

4269  {
4270  if ( get_PHP_only() == true )
4271  {
4272  frontendErrorLevel = build_PHP_AST();
4273  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel > 0);
4274  }
4275  else
4276  {
4277  if ( get_Java_only() == true )
4278  {
4279 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_JAVA_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
4280  //
4281  // PC 03/20/14 - This invocation of build_Java_AST will first invoke Javac (if the -rose:skip_syntax_check
4282  // option was not requested) to check whether or not the input is correct. In such a case,
4283  // if the input is incorrect then processing is stopped and the return code produced by javac
4284  // is returned here. If, on the other hand, the input is correct then processing continues with
4285  // an invocation of the Java-ROSE translator. When Java-ROSE detects a fatal error, it exits the
4286  // program instead of returning a code. Thus, only the javac error code ever reaches this point!
4287  // If the Java-ROSE translator encounters a recoverable error, it sets the ecjErrorCode to
4288  // indicate that an error was detected and continues with the translation.
4289  //
4290  // SUGGESTION: The fact that this arrangement requires so much explanation suggests that it's
4291  // not a good one. For clarity, I would have factored the syntax check out of the build_Java_AST
4292  // function like this:
4293  //
4294  // if (syntaxCheckInputCode == true) {
4295  // frontendErrorLevel = syntaxCheck(argv, inputCommandLine);
4296  // this -> set_javacErrorCode(frontendErrorLevel);
4297  // }
4298  // if (frontendErrorLevel == 0) { // if the syntax check was successful...
4299  // frontendErrorLevel = build_Java_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4300  // this -> set_ecjErrorCode(frontendErrorLevel);
4301  // /*
4302  // I still think it's prefarable to let the translator set this code rather than
4303  // having the C++ function (JavaParserActionRose.C) return a code to a Java
4304  // method (JavaTraversal.java) which in turn would return that code (indirectly)
4305  // to this function.
4306  // */
4307  // }
4308  //
4309  frontendErrorLevel = build_Java_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4310  this -> set_javacErrorCode(frontendErrorLevel);
4311  if (this->get_project()->get_keep_going() == false)
4312  {
4313  frontendErrorLevel = 0; // PC: Always keep going for Java!
4314  }
4315 #else
4316  // DQ (2/21/2016): Added "error: " to allow this to be caught by the ROSE Matrix Testing.
4317  ROSE_ASSERT (! "[FATAL] [ROSE] [frontend] [Java] "
4318  "error: ROSE was not configured to support the Java frontend.");
4319 #endif
4320 
4321  }
4322  else
4323  {
4324  if ( get_Python_only() == true )
4325  {
4326 #ifdef ROSE_BUILD_PYTHON_LANGUAGE_SUPPORT
4327  frontendErrorLevel = build_Python_AST();
4328  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel > 0);
4329 #else
4330  // DQ (2/21/2016): Added "error: " to allow this to be caught by the ROSE Matrix Testing.
4331  ROSE_ASSERT (! "[FATAL] [ROSE] [frontend] [Python] error: ROSE was not configured to support the Python frontend.");
4332 #endif
4333  }
4334  else
4335  {
4336  // DQ (8/25/2017): Added new langauge support.
4337  if (get_Csharp_only() == true)
4338  {
4339  frontendErrorLevel = build_Csharp_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4340  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel > 0);
4341  }
4342  else
4343  {
4344  // DQ (8/25/2017): Added new langauge support.
4345  if (get_Ada_only() == true)
4346  {
4347  frontendErrorLevel = build_Ada_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4348  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel > 0);
4349  }
4350  else
4351  {
4352  // DQ (8/25/2017): Added new langauge support.
4353  if (get_Jovial_only() == true)
4354  {
4355  frontendErrorLevel = build_Jovial_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4356  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel > 0);
4357  generateJovialCompoolFile(this);

4359  set_skipfinalCompileStep(true);

4361  else
4362  {
4363  // This is the C/C++ case (default).
4364  frontendErrorLevel = build_C_and_Cxx_AST(argv,inputCommandLine);
4365  // DQ (12/29/2008): The newer version of EDG (version 3.10 and 4.0) use different return codes for indicating an error.
4366  // Any non-zero value indicates an error.
4367  frontend_failed = (frontendErrorLevel != 0);
4368  }
4369  }
4370  }
4371  }
4372  }
4373  }
4374  }
4375 
4376  // Uniform processing of the error code!
4377 
4378  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
4379  printf ("DONE: frontend called (frontendErrorLevel = %d) \n",frontendErrorLevel);
4380 
4381  // If we had any errors reported by the frontend then quit now
4382  if (frontend_failed == true)
4383  {
4384  // cout << "Errors in Processing: (frontendErrorLevel > 3)" << endl;
4385  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
4386  printf ("frontendErrorLevel = %d \n",frontendErrorLevel);
4387 
4388  // DQ (9/22/2006): We need to invert the test result (return code) for
4389  // negative tests (where failure is expected and success is an error).
4390  if (get_negative_test() == true)
4391  {
4392  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
4393  {
4394  printf ("(evaluation of frontend results) This is a negative tests, so an error in compilation is a PASS but a successful \n");
4395  printf ("compilation is not a FAIL since the failure might happen in the compilation of the generated code by the vendor compiler. \n");
4396  }
4397  exit(0);
4398  }
4399  else
4400  {
4401  // DQ (1/28/2016): Tone this down a bit to be less sarcastic.
4402  // DQ (4/12/2015): Make this a more friendly message than what the OS provides on abort() (which is "Aborted (core dumped)").
4403  // Exit because there are errors in the input program
4404  // cout << "Errors in Processing: (frontend_failed)" << endl;
4405  // ROSE_ABORT("Errors in Processing: (frontend_failed)");
4406  // printf ("Errors in Processing Input File: (throwing an instance of \"frontend_failed\" exception due to errors detected in the input code), have a nice day! \n");
4407  printf ("Errors in Processing Input File: throwing an instance of \"frontend_failed\" exception due to syntax errors detected in the input code \n");
4408  if (Rose::KeepGoing::g_keep_going) {
4409  raise(SIGABRT); // raise a signal to be handled by the keep going support , instead of exit. Liao 4/25/2017
4410  }
4411  else
4412  exit(1);
4413  }
4414  }
4415 
4416  return frontendErrorLevel;
4417  }

4697  //

4702  if (returnValueForCompiler != 0)
4703  {
4704  this->set_backendCompilerErrorCode(-1);
4705  if (this->get_project()->get_keep_going() == true)
4706  {
4707  // 1. We already failed the compilation of the ROSE unparsed file.
4708  // 2. Now we tried to compile the original input file --
4709  // that was just compiled above -- and failed also.
4710  if (this->get_unparsedFileFailedCompilation())
4711  {
4712  this->set_backendCompilerErrorCode(-1);
4713  // TOO1 (11/16/2013): TODO: Allow user to catch InvalidOriginalInputFileException?
4714  //throw std::runtime_error("Original input file is invalid");
4715  std::cout << "[FATAL] "
4716  << "Original input file is invalid: "
4717  << "'" << this->getFileName() << "'"
4718  << "\n\treported by " << __FILE__ <<":"<<__LINE__ <<std::endl;
4719  if (Rose::KeepGoing::g_keep_going)
4720  raise(SIGABRT); // raise a signal to be handled by the keep going support , instead of exit. Liao 4/25/2017
4721  else
4722  exit(1);
4723  }
4724  else
4725  {
4726  // The ROSE unparsed file is invalid...
4727  this->set_frontendErrorCode(-1);
4728  this->set_unparsedFileFailedCompilation(true);
4729 
4730  returnValueForCompiler = this->compileOutput(argv, fileNameIndex);
4731  }
4732  }

4735  // depends on another file that has errors. We test for this condition by checking
4736  // whether or not the original input file compiles correctly with javac.
4737  //
4738  // Note that the fact that Javac fails on the original input does not prove that
4739  // the unparsed file is correct. It simply proves that the input file is incorrect.
4740  //
4741  else if (get_Java_only() == true) {
4742  compilerCmdLine[compilerCmdLine.size() - 1] = this -> get_sourceFileNameWithPath();
4743  int original_code = systemFromVector(compilerCmdLine);
4744  if (original_code != 0) { // The original file is erroneous too?
4745  returnValueForCompiler = 0;
4746  this->set_backendCompilerErrorCode(0);
4747  this -> set_ecjErrorCode(1); // Report this error as an ECJ error.
4748  }
4749  }
4750  }
4751 
4752  //
4753  // If we are processing Java, ...
4754  //
4755  if (get_Java_only() == true) {
4756  //
4757  // Report if an error detected only while compiling the output file?
4758  //
4759  if (this -> get_javacErrorCode() == 0 &&
4760  this -> get_ecjErrorCode() == 0 &&
4761  this -> get_frontendErrorCode() == 0 &&
4762  this -> get_project() -> get_midendErrorCode() == 0 &&
4763  this -> get_unparserErrorCode() == 0 &&
4764  this -> get_backendCompilerErrorCode() != 0) {
4765  cout << "ERROR found in output file: "
4766  << get_unparse_output_filename()
4767  << endl;
4768  }
4769 
4770  //
4771  // Report Error or Success of this translation.
4772  //
4773  if (this -> get_javacErrorCode() != 0) {
4774  cout << "Javac COMPILATION ERROR(s) found in "
4775  << this -> getFileName()
4776  << endl;
4777  cout.flush();
4778  }
4779  else if (this -> get_ecjErrorCode() != 0) {
4780  cout << "ECJ COMPILATION ERROR(s) found in "
4781  << this -> getFileName()
4782  << endl;
4783  cout.flush();
4784  }
4785  else if (this -> get_frontendErrorCode() != 0 ||
4786  this -> get_project() -> get_midendErrorCode() != 0 ||
4787  this -> get_unparserErrorCode() != 0 ||
4788  this -> get_backendCompilerErrorCode() != 0) {
4789  cout << "ERROR compiling "
4790  << this -> getFileName()
4791  << endl;
4792  cout.flush();
4793  }
4794  else {
4795  cout << "SUCCESS compiling "
4796  << this -> getFileName()
4797  << endl;
4798  cout.flush();
4799  }
4800 
4801  if (this->get_project()->get_keep_going() == false) {
4802  this -> set_javacErrorCode(0); // keep going !!!
4803  this -> set_ecjErrorCode(0); // keep going !!!
4804  this -> set_frontendErrorCode(0); // keep going !!!
4805  this -> set_unparserErrorCode(0); // keep going !!!
4806  this -> set_backendCompilerErrorCode(0); // keep going !!!
4807  }
4808  }
4809  }
4810  else
4811  {
4812  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
4813  printf ("COMPILER NOT CALLED: compilerNameString = %s \n", "<unknown>" /* compilerNameString.c_str() */);
4814 
4815  // DQ (8/21/2008): If this is a binary then we don't need the message output.
4816  // Liao 8/29/2008: disable it for non-verbose model
4817  if ( (get_binary_only() == false) && (get_verbose() > 0) )
4818  {
4819  printf ("Skipped call to backend vendor compiler! \n");
4820  }
4821  }
4822 
4823  // DQ (7/20/2006): Catch errors returned from unix "system" function
4824  // (commonly "out of memory" errors, suggested by Peter and Jeremiah).
4825  if (returnValueForCompiler < 0)
4826  {
4827  perror("Serious Error returned from internal systemFromVector command");
4828  }
4829 
4830  // Assemble an exit status that combines the values for ROSE and the C++/C compiler
4831  // return an exit status which is the boolean OR of the bits from the EDG/SAGE/ROSE and the compile step
4832  int finalCompiledExitStatus = returnValueForRose | returnValueForCompiler;
4833 
4834  // It is a strange property of the UNIX $status that it does not map uniformally from
4835  // the return value of the "exit" command (or "return" statement). So if the exit
4836  // status from the compilation stage is nonzero then we just make the exit status 1
4837  // (this does seem to be a portable solution).
4838  // FYI: only the first 8 bits of the exit value are significant (Solaris uses 'exit_value mod 256').
4839  if (finalCompiledExitStatus != 0)
4840  {
4841  // If this it is non-zero then make it 1 to be more clear to external tools (e.g. make)
4842  finalCompiledExitStatus = 1;
4843  }
4844 
4845  // DQ (9/19/2006): We need to invert the test result (return code) for
4846  // negative tests (where failure is expected and success is an error).
4847  if (get_negative_test() == true)
4848  {
4849  if ( get_verbose() > 1 )
4850  printf ("This is a negative tests, so an error in compilation is a PASS and successful compilation is a FAIL (vendor compiler return value = %d) \n",returnValueForCompiler);
4851 
4852  finalCompiledExitStatus = (finalCompiledExitStatus == 0) ? /* error */ 1 : /* success */ 0;
4853  }
4854 
4855  // Liao, 4/26/2017. KeepGoingTranslator should keep going no mater what.
4856  if (Rose::KeepGoing::g_keep_going)
4857  {
4858  finalCompiledExitStatus = 0;
4859  }
4860 
4861  return finalCompiledExitStatus;
4862  }

5125 #if DEBUG_PROJECT_COMPILE_COMMAND_LINE || 0

5141  if (KEEP_GOING_CAUGHT_BACKEND_COMPILER_SIGNAL)

5161  if (localErrorCode > errorCode)

5166  if (multifile_support_compile_only_flag == true)

5192

5209  if (get_compileOnly() == false)

5216 #if DEBUG_PROJECT_COMPILE_COMMAND_LINE

5218 #endif
5219  }
5220  }

5223  return errorCode + linkingReturnVal;

5258 // DQ (10/14/2010): Removing reference to macros defined in rose_config.h (defined in the header file as a default parameter).
5260 int SgProject::link(std::string linkerName)
5261  {
5262  // DQ (30/8/2017): Csharp does not include a concept of linking, as I understand it presently.
5263  if (get_Csharp_only() || get_Ada_only() || get_Jovial_only() || get_Jvm_only())
5264  {
5265  mlog[WARN] << "In SgProject::link(): language doesn't support linking, skipping the linking step\n";
5266  return 0;
5267  }
5268 
5269  if (numberOfFiles() == 0 && numberOfDirectories() == 0)
5270  {
5271  if (get_verbose() > 0)
5272  cout << "SgProject::link maybe encountering an object file ..." << endl;
5273 
5274  // DQ (1/24/2010): support for directories not in place yet.
5275  if (numberOfDirectories() > 0)
5276  {
5277  printf ("Directory support for linking not implemented... (unclear what this means...)\n");
5278  return 0;
5279  }
5280  }
5281  else
5282  {
5283  // normal cases that rose translators will actually do something about the input files
5284  // and we have SgFile for each of the files.
5285  if ( get_compileOnly() || get_file(0).get_skipfinalCompileStep() ||get_file(0).get_skip_unparse())
5286  {
5287  if (get_verbose() > 0)
5288  cout << "Skipping SgProject::link ..." << endl;
5289  return 0;
5290  }
5291  }
5292 
5293  // Compile the output file from the unparsing
5294  vector<string> argcArgvList = get_originalCommandLineArgumentList();
5295 
5296  // error checking
5297  if (numberOfFiles() != 0)
5298  ROSE_ASSERT (argcArgvList.size() > 1);
5299 
5300  ROSE_ASSERT(linkerName != "");
5301 
5302  // strip out any rose options before passing the command line.
5303  SgFile::stripRoseCommandLineOptions( argcArgvList );
5304 
5305  // strip out edg specific options that would cause an error in the backend linker (compiler).
5306  SgFile::stripEdgCommandLineOptions( argcArgvList );
5307 
5308  SgFile::stripTranslationCommandLineOptions( argcArgvList );
5309 
5310  // remove the original compiler/linker name
5311  if (argcArgvList.size() > 0) argcArgvList.erase(argcArgvList.begin());
5312 
5313  // remove all original file names
5314  Rose_STL_Container<string> sourceFilenames = get_sourceFileNameList();
5315  for (Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator i = sourceFilenames.begin(); i != sourceFilenames.end(); i++)
5316  {
5317 #if USE_ABSOLUTE_PATHS_IN_SOURCE_FILE_LIST
5318 #error "USE_ABSOLUTE_PATHS_IN_SOURCE_FILE_LIST is not supported yet"
5319  // DQ (9/1/2006): Check for use of absolute path and convert filename to absolute path if required
5320  bool usesAbsolutePath = ((*i)[0] == '/');
5321  if (usesAbsolutePath == false)
5322  {
5323  string targetSourceFileToRemove = StringUtility::getAbsolutePathFromRelativePath(*i);
5324  printf ("Converting source file to absolute path to search for it and remove it! targetSourceFileToRemove = %s \n",targetSourceFileToRemove.c_str());
5325  argcArgvList.remove(targetSourceFileToRemove);
5326  }
5327  else
5328  {
5329  argcArgvList.remove(*i);
5330  }
5331 #else
5332  if (find(argcArgvList.begin(),argcArgvList.end(),*i) != argcArgvList.end())
5333  {
5334  argcArgvList.erase(find(argcArgvList.begin(),argcArgvList.end(),*i));
5335  }
5336 #endif
5337  }
5338 
5339  // fix double quoted strings
5340  // DQ (4/14/2005): Fixup quoted strings in args fix "-DTEST_STRING_MACRO="Thu Apr 14 08:18:33 PDT 2005"
5341  // to be -DTEST_STRING_MACRO=\""Thu Apr 14 08:18:33 PDT 2005"\" This is a problem in the compilation of
5342  // a Kull file (version.cc), when the backend is specified as /usr/apps/kull/tools/mpig++-3.4.1. The
5343  // problem is that /usr/apps/kull/tools/mpig++-3.4.1 is a wrapper for a shell script /usr/local/bin/mpiCC
5344  // which does not tend to observe quotes well. The solution is to add additional escaped quotes.
5345  for (Rose_STL_Container<string>::iterator i = argcArgvList.begin(); i != argcArgvList.end(); i++)
5346  {
5347  std::string::size_type startingQuote = i->find("\"");
5348  if (startingQuote != std::string::npos)
5349  {
5350  std::string::size_type endingQuote = i->rfind("\"");
5351 
5352  // There should be a double quote on both ends of the string
5353  ROSE_ASSERT (endingQuote != std::string::npos);
5354 
5355  std::string quotedSubstring = i->substr(startingQuote,endingQuote);
5356 
5357  // DQ (11/1/2012): Robb has suggested using single quote instead of double quotes here.
5358  // This is a problem for the processing of mutt (large C application) (but we can figure
5359  // out the link command after the compile command).
5360  // std::string fixedQuotedSubstring = std::string("\\\"") + quotedSubstring + std::string("\\\"");
5361  // std::string fixedQuotedSubstring = std::string("\\\'") + quotedSubstring + std::string("\\\'");
5362  std::string fixedQuotedSubstring = std::string("\\\"") + quotedSubstring + std::string("\\\"");
5363 
5364  // Now replace the quotedSubstring with the fixedQuotedSubstring
5365  i->replace(startingQuote,endingQuote,fixedQuotedSubstring);
5366 
5367  printf ("Modified argument = %s \n",(*i).c_str());
5368  }
5369  }
5370 
5371  int errorCode = link(argcArgvList, linkerName);
5372  return errorCode;
5373  }

5375 int SgProject::link ( const std::vector<std::string>& argv, std::string linkerName )

5382  {

5391  {
5392  // linkerName = "f77 ";

5396  {

5399  {
5400  linkerName = BACKEND_JAVA_COMPILER_NAME_WITH_PATH;
5401 
5402  // Debugging support.

5404 
5405  // Java programs don't link so this is an error.

5409  else
5410  {
5411  // Nothing to do here (case of C++)
5412  }
5413  }

5417  Rose_STL_Container<string> linkingCommand;

5419  linkingCommand.push_back (linkerName);
5420  // find all object files generated at file level compilation
5421  // The assumption is that -o objectFileName is made explicit and
5422  // is generated by SgFile::generateOutputFileName()
5423  for (int i=0; i < numberOfFiles(); i++)

5428  if (get_file(i).get_skipfinalCompileStep() == false)

5430  linkingCommand.push_back(get_file(i).generateOutputFileName());

5438

5440  // There will be no SgFile at all in this case but we still want to append relevant linking options for OpenMP
5441  if (get_openmp_linking())

5662  {

5717 SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement*
5718 SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement::createDirective ( PreprocessingInfo* currentPreprocessingInfo )
5719  {
5720  // This is the new factory interface to build CPP directives as IR nodes.
5721  PreprocessingInfo::DirectiveType directive = currentPreprocessingInfo->getTypeOfDirective();
5722 
5723  // SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement* cppDirective = new SgEmptyDirectiveStatement();
5724  SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement* cppDirective = nullptr;
5725 
5726  switch(directive)
5727  {
5728  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration:
5729  {
5730  // I think this is an error...
5731  // locatedNode->addToAttachedPreprocessingInfo(currentPreprocessingInfoPtr);
5732  printf ("Error: directive == PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUnknownDeclaration \n");
5733  ROSE_ABORT();
5734  }
5735 
5736  case PreprocessingInfo::C_StyleComment:
5737  case PreprocessingInfo::CplusplusStyleComment:
5738  case PreprocessingInfo::FortranStyleComment:
5739  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorBlankLine:
5740  case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationStart:
5741  case PreprocessingInfo::ClinkageSpecificationEnd:
5742  {
5743  printf ("Error: these cases could not generate a new IR node (directiveTypeName = %s) \n",PreprocessingInfo::directiveTypeName(directive).c_str());
5744  ROSE_ABORT();
5745  }
5746 
5747  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIncludeDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIncludeDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5748  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIncludeNextDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIncludeNextDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5749  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDefineDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgDefineDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5750  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorUndefDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgUndefDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5751  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfdefDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIfdefDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5752  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfndefDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIfndefDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5753  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIfDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIfDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5754  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorDeadIfDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgDeadIfDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5755  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorElseDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgElseDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5756  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorElifDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgElseifDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5757  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorEndifDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgEndifDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5758  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorLineDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgLineDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5759  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorErrorDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgErrorDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5760  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorWarningDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgWarningDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5761  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorEmptyDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgEmptyDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5762  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorIdentDeclaration: { cppDirective = new SgIdentDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5763  case PreprocessingInfo::CpreprocessorCompilerGeneratedLinemarker: { cppDirective = new SgLinemarkerDirectiveStatement(); break; }
5764 
5765  default:
5766  {
5767  printf ("Error: directive not handled directiveTypeName = %s \n",PreprocessingInfo::directiveTypeName(directive).c_str());
5768  ROSE_ABORT();
5769  }
5770  }
5771 
5772  ASSERT_not_null(cppDirective);
5773 
5774  printf ("In SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement::createDirective(): currentPreprocessingInfo->getString() = %s \n",currentPreprocessingInfo->getString().c_str());
5775 
5776  cppDirective->set_directiveString(currentPreprocessingInfo->getString());
5777 
5778  printf ("In SgC_PreprocessorDirectiveStatement::createDirective(): cppDirective->get_directiveString() = %s \n",cppDirective->get_directiveString().c_str());
5779 
5780  // Set the defining declaration to be a self reference...
5781  cppDirective->set_definingDeclaration(cppDirective);
5782 
5783  // Build source position information...
5784  cppDirective->set_startOfConstruct(new Sg_File_Info(*(currentPreprocessingInfo->get_file_info())));
5785  cppDirective->set_endOfConstruct (new Sg_File_Info(*(currentPreprocessingInfo->get_file_info())));
5786 
5787  return cppDirective;
5788  }

5790 bool
5791 StringUtility::popen_wrapper ( const string & command, vector<string> & result )
5792  {
5793  // DQ (2/5/2009): Simple wrapper for Unix popen command.
5794 
5795  const int SIZE = 10000;
5796  bool returnValue = true;
5797  FILE* fp = nullptr;
5798  char buffer[SIZE];
5799 
5800  result = vector<string>();
5801 
5802  // CH (4/6/2010): The Windows version of popen is _popen
5803 #ifdef _MSC_VER
5804  if ((fp = _popen(command.c_str (), "r")) == nullptr)
5805 #else
5806  if ((fp = popen(command.c_str (), "r")) == nullptr)
5807 #endif
5808  {
5809  cerr << "Files or processes cannot be created" << endl;
5810  returnValue = false;
5811  return returnValue;
5812  }
5813 
5814  string current_string;
5815  while (fgets(buffer, sizeof (buffer), fp))
5816  {
5817  current_string = buffer;
5818  if (current_string [current_string.size () - 1] != '\n')
5819  {
5820  cerr << "SIZEBUF too small (" << SIZE << ")" << endl;
5821  returnValue = false;
5822  return returnValue;
5823  }
5824  ROSE_ASSERT(current_string [current_string.size () - 1] == '\n');
5825  result.push_back (current_string.substr (0, current_string.size () - 1));
5826  }
5827 
5828 #ifdef _MSC_VER
5829  if (_pclose(fp) == -1)
5830 #else
5831  if (pclose(fp) == -1)
5832 #endif
5833  {
5834  cerr << ("Cannot execute pclose");
5835  returnValue = false;
5836  }
5837 
5838  return returnValue;
5839  }

5890 SgFunctionSymbol*
5891 SgFunctionCallExp::getAssociatedFunctionSymbol() const
5892  {
5893  // This is helpful in chasing down the associated declaration to this function reference.
5894  // But this refactored function does the first step of getting the symbol, so that it
5895  // can also be used separately in the outlining support.
5896  SgFunctionSymbol* returnSymbol = nullptr;
5897 
5898  // Note that as I recall there are a number of different types of IR nodes that
5899  // the functionCallExp->get_function() can return (this is the complete list,
5900  // as tested in astConsistancyTests.C):
5901  // - SgDotExp
5902  // - SgDotStarOp
5903  // - SgArrowExp
5904  // - SgArrowStarOp
5905  // - SgPointerDerefExp
5906  // - SgAddressOfOp
5907  // - SgFunctionRefExp
5908  // - SgMemberFunctionRefExp
5909  // - SgFunctionSymbol // Liao 4/7/2017, discovered by a call to RAJA template functions using lambda expressions
5910  // schroder3 (2016-06-28): There are some more (see below).
5911 
5912  // Some virtual functions are resolved statically (e.g. for objects allocated on the stack)
5913  bool isAlwaysResolvedStatically = false;
5914 
5915  SgExpression* functionExp = this->get_function();
5916 
5917  // schroder3 (2016-08-16): Moved the handling of SgPointerDerefExp and SgAddressOfOp above the switch. Due to this
5918  // all pointer dereferences and address-ofs are removed from the function expression before it is analyzed.
5919  // Member functions that are an operand of a pointer dereference or address-of are supported due to this now.
5920  //
5921  // schroder3 (2016-06-28): Added SgAddressOp (for example "(&f)()", "(*&***&**&*&f)()" or "(&***&**&*&f)()")
5922  //
5923  // EDG3 removes all SgPointerDerefExp nodes from an expression like this
5924  // void f() { (***f)(); }
5925  // EDG4 does not. Therefore, if the thing to which the pointers ultimately point is a SgFunctionRefExp then we
5926  // know the function, otherwise Liao's comment below applies. [Robb Matzke 2012-12-28]
5927  //
5928  // Liao, 5/19/2009
5929  // A pointer to function can be associated to any functions with a matching function type
5930  // There is no single function declaration which is associated with it.
5931  // In this case return NULL should be allowed and the caller has to handle it accordingly
5932  //
5933  while (isSgPointerDerefExp(functionExp) || isSgAddressOfOp(functionExp)) {
5934  functionExp = isSgUnaryOp(functionExp)->get_operand();
5935  }
5936 
5937  switch (functionExp->variantT())
5938  {
5939  case V_SgPointerDerefExp:
5940  case V_SgAddressOfOp:
5941  {
5942  ROSE_ABORT();
5943  }
5944  case V_SgFunctionRefExp:
5945  {
5946  SgFunctionRefExp* functionRefExp = isSgFunctionRefExp(functionExp);
5947  ASSERT_not_null(functionRefExp);
5948  returnSymbol = functionRefExp->get_symbol();
5949 
5950  // DQ (2/8/2009): Can we assert this! What about pointers to functions?
5951  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
5952  break;
5953  }
5954 
5955  // DQ (2/24/2013): Added case to support SgTemplateFunctionRefExp (now generated as a result of
5956  // work on 2/23/2013 specific to unknown function handling in templates, now resolved by name).
5957  case V_SgTemplateFunctionRefExp:
5958  {
5959  SgTemplateFunctionRefExp* functionRefExp = isSgTemplateFunctionRefExp(functionExp);
5960  ASSERT_not_null(functionRefExp);
5961  returnSymbol = functionRefExp->get_symbol();
5962 
5963  // DQ (2/8/2009): Can we assert this! What about pointers to functions?
5964  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
5965  break;
5966  }
5967 
5968  // DQ (2/25/2013): Added case to support SgTemplateFunctionRefExp (now generated as a result of
5969  // work on 2/23/2013 specific to unknown function handling in templates, now resolved by name).
5970  case V_SgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp:
5971  {
5972  SgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp* templateMemberFunctionRefExp = isSgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp(functionExp);
5973  ASSERT_not_null(templateMemberFunctionRefExp);
5974  returnSymbol = templateMemberFunctionRefExp->get_symbol();
5975 
5976  // DQ (2/8/2009): Can we assert this! What about pointers to functions?
5977  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
5978  break;
5979  }
5980 
5981  case V_SgMemberFunctionRefExp:
5982  {
5983  SgMemberFunctionRefExp* memberFunctionRefExp = isSgMemberFunctionRefExp(functionExp);
5984  ASSERT_not_null(memberFunctionRefExp);
5985  returnSymbol = memberFunctionRefExp->get_symbol();
5986 
5987  // DQ (2/8/2009): Can we assert this! What about pointers to functions?
5988  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
5989  break;
5990  }
5991 
5992  case V_SgArrowExp:
5993  {
5994  // The lhs is the this pointer (SgThisExp) and the rhs is the member function.
5995  SgArrowExp* arrayExp = isSgArrowExp(functionExp);
5996  ASSERT_not_null(arrayExp);
5997 
5998  SgMemberFunctionRefExp* memberFunctionRefExp = isSgMemberFunctionRefExp(arrayExp->get_rhs_operand());
5999 
6000  // DQ (2/21/2010): Relaxed this constraint because it failes in fixupPrettyFunction test.
6001  // ROSE_ASSERT(memberFunctionRefExp != NULL);
6002  if (memberFunctionRefExp != nullptr)
6003  {
6004  returnSymbol = memberFunctionRefExp->get_symbol();
6005 
6006  // DQ (2/8/2009): Can we assert this! What about pointers to functions?
6007  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
6008  }
6009  break;
6010  }
6011 
6012  case V_SgDotExp:
6013  {
6014  SgDotExp * dotExp = isSgDotExp(functionExp);
6015  ASSERT_not_null(dotExp);
6016  ASSERT_not_null(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6017 #if 0
6018  printf ("In SgFunctionCallExp::getAssociatedFunctionSymbol(): case V_SgDotExp: dotExp->get_rhs_operand() = %p = %s \n",dotExp->get_rhs_operand(),dotExp->get_rhs_operand()->class_name().c_str());
6019 #endif
6020  // There are four different types of function call reference expression in ROSE.
6021  SgMemberFunctionRefExp* memberFunctionRefExp = isSgMemberFunctionRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6022  if (memberFunctionRefExp == nullptr)
6023  {
6024  // This could be a SgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp (not derived from SgMemberFunctionRefExp or SgFunctionRefExp). See test2013_70.C
6025  SgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp* templateMemberFunctionRefExp = isSgTemplateMemberFunctionRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6026  if (templateMemberFunctionRefExp == nullptr)
6027  {
6028  SgTemplateFunctionRefExp* templateFunctionRefExp = isSgTemplateFunctionRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6029  if (templateFunctionRefExp == nullptr)
6030  {
6031  SgFunctionRefExp* functionRefExp = isSgFunctionRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6032  if (functionRefExp == nullptr)
6033  {
6034  SgVarRefExp* varRefExp = isSgVarRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6035  if (varRefExp == nullptr)
6036  {
6037  SgNonrealRefExp* nrRefExp = isSgNonrealRefExp(dotExp->get_rhs_operand());
6038  if (nrRefExp == nullptr) {
6039  dotExp->get_rhs_operand()->get_file_info()->display("In SgFunctionCallExp::getAssociatedFunctionSymbol(): case of SgDotExp: templateMemberFunctionRefExp == NULL: debug");
6040  printf ("In SgFunctionCallExp::getAssociatedFunctionSymbol(): case of SgDotExp: dotExp->get_rhs_operand() = %p = %s \n",dotExp->get_rhs_operand(),dotExp->get_rhs_operand()->class_name().c_str());
6041  } else {
6042  // FIXME should we return the non-real symbol?
6043  }
6044  }
6045  else
6046  {
6047  ASSERT_not_null(varRefExp);
6048 
6049  // DQ (8/20/2013): This is not a SgFunctionSymbol so we can't return a valid symbol from this case of a function call from a pointer to a function.
6050  // returnSymbol = varRefExp->get_symbol();
6051  }
6052  }
6053  else
6054  {
6055  // I am unclear when this is possible, but STL code exercises it.
6056  ASSERT_not_null(functionRefExp);
6057  returnSymbol = functionRefExp->get_symbol();
6058 
6059  ASSERT_not_null(returnSymbol);
6060  }
6061  }
6062  else
6063  {
6064  // I am unclear when this is possible, but STL code exercises it.
6065  ASSERT_not_null(templateFunctionRefExp);
